reverified.title: Unvalidated whatsup.logbook.v1 shape: any mismatch throws inside the feed callback, which kills the feed permanently (no retry, no reset path)
reasons:
REFUTED: The failure path itself is real: a throw in updateLog at web/model.mjs:218 escapes onUpdate inside poll() at web/live.mjs:324/326. That rejects the async poll before setTimeout at line 327, so polling would stop. But I found no realistic way to trigger it.

1. The app is the only writer of whatsup.logbook.v1. It writes the key only at model.mjs:218 with updateLog's own output, and the key lives in the app-private WebView localStorage.
2. Every version in git history writes the same day, seen, typesAll and cargo{night,seen} fields. That covers e5df0be, 3954b39 and the current code. updateLog also migrates older shapes in place: a missing planes field is rebuilt from typesToday, typesZone/zoneSeen are deleted, and an array cargo.seen is replaced.
3. Corrupt JSON cannot reach updateLog, because store.get (live.mjs:62) wraps JSON.parse in try/catch and returns null.
4. Any valid-JSON value that is a primitive, an array, or an object for a different or missing day fails the `log.day!==day` check at model.mjs:84. The log is then rebuilt with safe defaults (`log?.typesAll||{}`, `log?.cargo||{...}`).
5. The only input that throws is a hand-made object for the current local day that is missing seen, cargo or typesAll. Nothing in the app can produce it; it would need someone with devtools or ADB editing private WebView storage.

Even then the effect is not permanent. At the next local midnight the day check fails and the log is rebuilt from defaults. A restart does not clear it, but the first-run reset (resetLog at app.mjs:171) does.

The unguarded onUpdate inside poll() is a fair hardening item: a try/catch around onUpdate, or scheduling the next poll in finally, would protect the feed from any future throw in the model. As written, though, the logbook claim does not reproduce.

REFUTED: The crash mechanism is real, but nothing in the code can set it off. model.mjs:143 does run cargoCounts(log.cargo.seen) on whatever liveSource loads with store.get(LOG_KEY) (model.mjs:204). If that throws inside onUpdate, poll() in live.mjs:312-327 rejects before it reaches setTimeout, so polling would stop.

The trigger, though, is a stored whatsup.logbook.v1 with a different shape, and nothing produces one:
(1) The app is the only writer of this key (model.mjs:220, store.set after updateLog), and the value round-trips through JSON.
(2) Every version of updateLog since the first commit that wrote the key (e5df0be) builds the object with day, seen, highest, fastest, typesToday, typesAll and cargo{night,seen}.
(3) The later shape changes are migrated in updateLog: missing planes is rebuilt from typesToday, an array cargo.seen is replaced and stale typesZone/zoneSeen are deleted.
(4) pickRarest and pickFarthest already use optional chaining (log?.planes||{}), and logSummary returns early when log is null.
(5) There is a reset path: app.mjs:171 calls resetLog() when home changes, and localStorage writes are atomic, so a partial write can't leave a half-shaped object.

Getting a valid-JSON value of the wrong shape needs an outside edit to localStorage or a future schema change. That makes this defensive hardening (wrap the loaded log in a shape check or try/catch), not a concrete defect.

REFUTED: The mechanism holds up, but there is no realistic way to trigger it. If logSummary or updateLog threw, the throw would happen inside onUpdate, which poll() calls before setTimeout(poll) (live.mjs:320-323). Polling would stop, and the initial onUpdate(states,false) at live.mjs:325 would also throw from start(). The problem is getting a bad shape into whatsup.logbook.v1 in the first place. (1) The only writer is liveSource itself (model.mjs:218), which stores the result of updateLog. updateLog always builds a complete object {day,seen,planes,highest,fastest,typesToday,typesAll,cargo:{night,seen}}. It also normalizes cargo (line 91) and migrates older logs that have no planes (line 88). (2) I checked every commit that writes this key (e5df0be, 1894c78, e462e19 through HEAD). All of them write the same cargo/seen shape, so an older stored version cannot leave an incompatible log behind. (3) store.get (live.mjs:62) wraps JSON.parse in try/catch. Truncated or corrupt JSON comes back as null (or the in-memory copy), and logSummary(null) and updateLog(null) both handle null safely. (4) The page is file:///pkg/assets/index.html. Only this app's code shares that localStorage origin, and the user has no way to edit it on a Fire TV. A shape mismatch would therefore need a future developer to change the schema without a migration, and that is a hypothetical, not a defect in the shipped code. One recovery path also exists: choosing a new place (applyPlace with fresh) calls resetLog(). Hardening still has some value: wrapping the onUpdate call in poll(), or the logbook step, in try/catch would keep any future throw from killing the feed. But the logbook-shape trigger the claim depends on is not reachable from the code as written.

reverified.title: store.set swallows QuotaExceededError with no eviction, and store.get then returns the stale persisted value instead of the in-memory one
reasons:
REFUTED: The mechanism exists but does no visible harm. In web/live.mjs:62-63, set() writes to the in-memory map first and silently ignores a failed localStorage.setItem. get() reads localStorage first, so after a quota failure it would return an older persisted value if one exists. But no caller reads back a value it just wrote, and the one that does checks what it gets:
- Settings: app.mjs:27 calls loadSettings() once at startup, and the session keeps `settings` in memory. The only other reload is app.mjs:657 (?reset=1), which writes {}, a tiny value. A failed save never leads to a stale read in the same session.
- History, ledger and log (live.mjs:275-276, model.mjs:204) are read once at start and then kept in memory variables.
- savedMap (mapgen.mjs:213-217, called at app.mjs:176) can read back an older map after saveMap fails. That map is only accepted if the version, range, home position (within 0.01 degrees) and age (under MAX_AGE) all match. So the result is either a still-valid map for the same home or null, which just triggers a rebuild.
- The large items, the detail maps of about 0.8 MB, skip `store` entirely (mapgen.mjs:351-366). They have their own handling for a full quota: remove the slot and return false.
Hitting the quota at all is also unlikely, since the comments say the map payloads are sized to stay under it. What is left is a quieter issue: if the quota is full, a settings change is lost at the next launch, with no error shown. That is low-impact and not the claimed bug.

REFUTED: The code does behave as described. In web/live.mjs:62-63, set() writes to the in-memory map first and then calls localStorage.setItem. If setItem throws (QuotaExceededError), the browser leaves the old value in localStorage, and get() reads localStorage before the in-memory map, so it returns the old value. But no caller re-reads a key after writing it in a way that shows the user anything wrong.

1) Settings (web/place.mjs:58, 73): loadSettings() runs only at startup (web/app.mjs:27) and in the ?reset=1 path (web/app.mjs:657). During a session the in-memory `settings` object in app.mjs is what the app uses, and saveSettings never triggers a re-read.
2) Ledger, history and log (web/live.mjs:275-276, web/model.mjs:204): each is read once at startup, then kept in local variables and only written after that.
3) savedMap (web/mapgen.mjs:213-218) does re-read, but it checks version, range, distance from home and age before using the map. A value left behind by a failed write is one that failed those checks, which is why it was rebuilt, so it fails them again and the result is null and a rebuild, not stale data on screen.
4) The large item that could actually fill the quota, the detail map, does not go through `store`. It writes to localStorage itself and removes its own key if the write fails (web/mapgen.mjs:351-365). Its buildings are also capped to stay under the quota.

The only remaining effect is that a failed write does not survive a restart, which is the stated design ("memory for this launch only"). This is a latent pattern with no reachable impact. A harmless hardening would be to call localStorage.removeItem(k) in set()'s catch so get() falls back to the in-memory value.

REFUTED: The mechanism is real, but the claimed impact doesn't happen in this app. At web/live.mjs:62-63, store.set does write memory first and then swallows a localStorage.setItem failure. store.get does check localStorage before memory, so after a failed set it would return the older persisted value. The problem is that almost no caller reads a key back after writing it in the same session:
- Settings are loaded once into a module variable (web/app.mjs:27, `let settings=loadSettings()`). Every change edits that in-memory object and then calls saveSettings, and loadSettings is never called again.
- The route ledger and history (web/live.mjs:275-276) and the logbook (web/model.mjs:204) are each read once at startup and kept in local variables after that. store.get is never called on them again.
- The only read-after-write path is savedMap (web/mapgen.mjs:214), reached from web/app.mjs:176. It checks whatever it gets back for version, range, distance from home within 0.01 degrees, and age under 30 days. A stale entry is therefore either a still-valid older map of the same home (harmless) or null, which just triggers a rebuild. The user never sees wrong data.
- The largest storage user, the detail map, does not go through store. saveDetail (web/mapgen.mjs:362-366) catches the quota error and removes its own key. saveMap also evicts all but the 3 most recent saved maps (web/mapgen.mjs:221). So "no eviction" overstates it.

The only real consequence is that if storage is already full, a settings or history change is not persisted and is lost on the next launch. Nothing becomes stale or wrong during the session. Reaching the quota from these small keys plus 3 capped maps is speculative and not shown. That is at most a minor hardening item for a TV user, not P2.

reverified.title: Alert-zone toggle removes HISTORY_KEY while the old feed is still polling for 900 ms, so the old list is written back and survives the restart
reasons:
UPHELD: This defect is real, and P3 is the right severity. At web/app.mjs:324, toggling the zone runs store.remove(HISTORY_KEY) and then zoneChanged(). zoneChanged() only schedules restartFeed after 900 ms (app.mjs:360), and every press resets that timer. Until restartFeed calls feed.stop() (app.mjs:163-167), the old startLive closure keeps running. It still holds its in-memory `history`, loaded from storage at web/live.mjs:276, and it still uses the old zone shape (live.mjs:278).

The old list gets written back in two ways:
- A poll that fires inside the 900 ms window. Polls run every 5 s at small radius (config.js:7; app.mjs:38).
- A poll whose request was already in flight. These have a 4 s timeout, and the check at live.mjs:315 only looks at `stopped`, which is still false.

If either poll finds any plane inside the old zone, live.mjs:320 runs history=mergeHistory(history,sel.inside) and then store.set(HISTORY_KEY,history). That writes back the full old list plus newly classified old-shape entries. When restartFeed runs, the new startLive reads store.get(HISTORY_KEY) at live.mjs:276 and gets that list back. So the "Recently above" list the toggle meant to clear survives, still showing the other zone shape.

Odds per toggle are roughly 20-30% while a plane is in the old zone, and repeated presses widen the window. The impact is cosmetic and temporary: stale history entries, capped at 20 and eventually aged out.

Suggested fix: in the set-zone branch, call feed?.stop() (or restartFeed()) before store.remove(HISTORY_KEY). Alternatively, clear history inside restartFeed when the zone kind changed.

UPHELD: I could not refute this; the race is real. At web/app.mjs:324, toggling the alert zone removes HISTORY_KEY right away. zoneChanged() then waits 900 ms before calling restartFeed (app.mjs:360), and restartFeed is what stops the old feed (app.mjs:165). Nothing stops or resets that feed earlier.

The old feed (web/live.mjs:276) keeps its own copy of `history`, read once at start. If any of its polls finishes in that window, and an in-flight request that started before the toggle counts, it runs `history=mergeHistory(history,sel.inside);store.set(HISTORY_KEY,history)` (live.mjs:320). That writes the full old list back, plus the planes that were inside the old zone shape. The `stopped` check does not help, because stop() is only called 900 ms later. The window is longer than 900 ms when the user presses the key repeatedly, since each press resets the timer. The new feed then reads the restored list at live.mjs:276, so "Recently above" keeps planes from the previous zone shape. The comment on line 324 says this is exactly what the remove is meant to prevent.

The trigger needs a poll to finish inside that window (polls run every CONFIG.pollSeconds, or 10 to 15 s for large search radii) and at least one plane inside the old zone at that moment. So it happens sometimes, not every time. The impact is cosmetic and goes away by itself as the list fills with new sightings (it keeps 20 rows). There is no crash and no data loss.

Suggested fix: in the set-zone branch, stop the feed right away (`feed?.stop();feed=null;`) before `store.remove(HISTORY_KEY)`. Alternatively, have restartFeed take a flag and clear HISTORY_KEY after the old feed has stopped, as applyPlace already does at app.mjs:170-171. P3 is the right severity.

UPHELD: The race is real, and P3 is the right severity. At app.mjs:324, toggling the alert zone calls store.remove(HISTORY_KEY) and then zoneChanged(). zoneChanged only schedules restartFeed after 900 ms (app.mjs:360), and every further key press pushes that timer back. Until then the old feed keeps running. Its startLive closure still holds the full in-memory `history` and the old `zone`. If a poll lands in that window (pollSeconds is 5 to 15 s, and a request already in flight also counts) and any plane is inside the old zone, live.mjs:320 runs history=mergeHistory(history,sel.inside) and then store.set(HISTORY_KEY,history). That writes the whole old list back, plus any new entry judged against the old shape. restartFeed (app.mjs:163-166) does not clear history, unlike applyPlace with fresh=true at line 171. The new feed then reads the restored list at live.mjs:276. So the clear is fully undone. For a TV user the impact is small and only cosmetic. After switching from "All around" to "Window view", the "Recently above" list (up to 20 rows) may still show planes that never crossed the window. The list corrects itself as new sightings push old rows out. There is no crash, no wrong live alert, and no chime effect. The odds are moderate: about 0.9 s plus any in-flight request against a 5 s poll, and only when a plane is inside at that moment. Fix: stop the old feed right away on a zone toggle (feed?.stop();feed=null; before or together with store.remove), or move the store.remove(HISTORY_KEY) into the delayed restart, after feed.stop().

reverified.title: enrich() has no `stopped` check after its await, so a stopped feed still emits one onUpdate and one logbook/ledger write after restartFeed/applyPlace
reasons:
UPHELD: I could not refute this. The bug path is real. In web/live.mjs:292-303, enrich() awaits enricher.tick(), which can wait up to 8 s on the adsb.lol request through getJson(url,8000). After that await it calls store.set(LEDGER_KEY,ledger) and onUpdate(states,true) without checking `stopped`. stop() (line 331) only sets stopped=true and clears the poll timer, so an enrich that is already running finishes. poll() checks `stopped` after each of its awaits (lines 316, 322), but it starts enrich at line 325 without awaiting it.

The callers are real:
- app.mjs:165 restartFeed and app.mjs:170 applyPlace both call feed.stop() and then start a new feed. In the non-demo path, applyPlace calls startFeed() synchronously (line 180).
- When the old enrich finishes, the old liveSource callback (model.mjs:205-222) runs. ok=true sets lastOk, so `fresh` is true. It then writes the old closure's `log` to LOG_KEY with store.set (line 218), then calls onModel, which is app render(). render() runs listen(m) and draw(m) with the old feed's planes. Those planes are recomputed against the module-global HOME, which start() has already moved to the new place.

Effects:
- A stale or wrongly placed frame is drawn, and listen/chime may run on it.
- After applyPlace(...,{fresh:true}) calls resetLog(), the old logbook comes back in storage until the new feed's next fresh update overwrites it.
- The old ledger snapshot overwrites LEDGER_KEY. This is transient, because the new feed rewrites the ledger on its own enrich.

All effects are brief and fix themselves on the next poll, so P3 is right. Fix: add `if(stopped)return;` right after the await in enrich(), before the ledger write and onUpdate.

UPHELD: The claim holds. In web/live.mjs:292-303, enrich() awaits enricher.tick(), which can wait up to 8 s on the adsb.lol route request through getJson(url,8000). After that await it has no `stopped` check: it writes LEDGER_KEY when the ledger is dirty and calls onUpdate(states,true). poll() is guarded after each of its awaits (lines 313/316/322), but enrich() is fired without being awaited at line 325, so stop() (line 331) cannot cancel it.

Nothing downstream filters the stale call. In web/model.mjs:205-221 the old liveSource closure runs, computes `fresh` as true because lastOk is recent, and runs `store.set(LOG_KEY,log)` with the old feed's in-memory logbook. It then calls onModel, which is app.mjs render() at line 160. render() has no feed or token check: restartFeed() (app.mjs:163) and applyPlace() (app.mjs:168) only call feed.stop().

Concrete trigger: change place in Settings (applyPlace(place,{fresh:true}), app.mjs:216/689) while a route lookup is in flight. applyPlace calls stop(), then resetLog() deletes LOG_KEY. During the buildMap await (app.mjs:183+) the stale enrich resolves, writes the old place's logbook back to storage and renders one frame of the old place's planes. When the new feed starts, liveSource reads that restored logbook (model.mjs:204), so the new place's "today" stats include the old place's sightings for the rest of the day. The stale ledger write is mostly harmless, because the new feed has already loaded its own Ledger and overwrites the stored copy on its next dirty write.

The impact is small and timing-dependent, and it lasts at most until the day rolls over or the next update. P3 is the right severity. Fix: add `if(stopped)return;` right after the await in enrich(), before the ledger write and onUpdate.

UPHELD: I could not refute the mechanism. In web/live.mjs:292-303, enrich() awaits enricher.tick(). That await can block on a ROUTE_URL getJson for up to 8s plus a 2s bridge margin. After the await, enrich() writes store.set(LEDGER_KEY, ledger) and calls onUpdate(states,true) without checking `stopped`. poll() does check `stopped` after each await; enrich() is the only path that doesn't. stop() (line 331) only sets the flag and clears the timer, so an enrich already in flight keeps running.

Trigger: change place, alert radius or zone (applyPlace or restartFeed, app.mjs:163-176) while a route lookup is pending. The old closure's onUpdate then runs the model.mjs:205 callback. Its own lastOk is recent, so `fresh` is true, and it calls render(), which runs draw() and listen(). That draws one frame of the old feed's planes, measured from the old home and radius, over the new map. It also seeds the reset chime gate with the old inside count. On applyPlace(fresh:true), it writes the old place's logbook back to LOG_KEY right after resetLog().

The impact on a TV user is small and does not last. The new feed is built synchronously in applyPlace/restartFeed before the old enrich resolves. It has already read the empty log and ledger, and it overwrites LOG_KEY and LEDGER_KEY on its next fresh update or dirty enrich, a few seconds later (pollSeconds is 5-15). So the bad data survives only if the app is killed in that gap. The stale frame is replaced on the next poll. chimeGate only sets ready=true on its first fresh call and never rings then, so the stale update cannot ring the chime by itself. In the worst case it could suppress or misjudge one later chime.

The defect is real, cosmetic and short-lived, and it needs a narrow timing window. P3 fits. Fix: add `if(stopped)return;` right after the await in enrich(), before the ledger write and onUpdate.

confirmed.title: Layout picker: returning to the current layout (Left after Right, or Back to cancel) while the preview is still loading leaves the previewed layout on screen
confirmed.trigger: Open Settings > Layout (picker). Press Right: stepPick calls useLayout(B), which starts an async loadLayout (a new script tag plus a stylesheet link, because unloadExcept dropped every other layout). Before it finishes, press Left to go back to the current layout A, or press Back to cancel. Either way useLayout(A) runs while active.id is still A. Pressing OK at that point (endPick(true) -> useLayout(A)) has the same effect.
confirmed.impact: useLayout returns at `if(active?.id===id)return;` before it increments layoutToken. The pending load of B therefore still matches `token===layoutToken` (line 103) and mounts B. After a cancel, the dashboard shows layout B while settings.layout and the Settings row still say A, and B only reverts on the next launch. With Left, the picker bar reads 'Layout 1 of 12 · Atlas Dark' over a different layout, and OK saves A while B stays mounted. Nothing gates input here: useLayout only shows the cog class and never sets busyNow, so a quick Right-then-Left is enough. The code itself notes that a layout switch 'can take a moment on the stick'.
confirmed.evidence: Lines 95-103: `id=validLayout(id); if(active?.id===id)return; const token=++layoutToken; ... mod=await loadLayout(id) ... if(token!==layoutToken)return;`. stepPick (line 425) calls useLayout(LAYOUTS[pick.index][0]) on every arrow press. endPick(false) (line 434) calls useLayout(settings.layout), which is still the active id while the preview loads.
confirmed.fix: Bump the token before the early return, so any in-flight load is invalidated: `const token=++layoutToken; if(active?.id===id){$('busy').classList.remove('on');return;}`. Another option is to keep a `loading` id and compare against both the active and loading ids.
reasons:
UPHELD: The bug is real. I confirmed it in web/app.mjs.

- **Early return skips the token bump.** useLayout (lines 95-103) checks `if(active?.id===id)return;` before `++layoutToken`.
- **Every picker arrow starts a load.** stepPick (lines 426-429) calls useLayout on each press.
- **Cancel and OK both re-request the current layout.** endPick(false) calls useLayout(settings.layout). Between the time the preview starts loading and the time it mounts, that is still active.id. endPick(true) after stepping back to A does the same.
- **The load is always async.** After unloadExcept removes the other layouts from the registry, loadLayout adds a script tag (bundled build; scripts/build-web.mjs sets __whatsupModules) and a stylesheet link, then waits for their onload. Even variants that share code (atlas, atlas-dark) still wait for a CSS link onload. So the pending load of B always resolves later.
- **The stale load still mounts.** When B resolves, `token===layoutToken` still holds because nothing bumped it, so B mounts.
- **No input gate.** The keydown handler (line 602) only blocks while busyNow is set, and useLayout never sets it. The busy cog does not block input. Right-then-Left or Right-then-Back during the load reproduces the bug.

Result: the dashboard shows B while settings.layout and the picker or Settings show A. B stays until the next useLayout call or the next launch.

Suggested fix: bump the token before the equality check, and clear the busy cog in that branch.

UPHELD: The race is real. In web/app.mjs:95-103, useLayout(id) returns at `if(active?.id===id)return;` before `++layoutToken`. Here is the sequence with A active:
1. Right calls stepPick(+1), which runs useLayout(B) and gets token N.
2. While loadLayout(B) is still pending, Left (stepPick(-1)) or Back/cancel (endPick(false), lines 254, 262 and 436) calls useLayout(A). active.id is still A, so it returns right away and the token stays N.
3. B's load resolves, `token!==layoutToken` is false, and B is mounted with `active={id:B}`. settings.layout still says A, and the picker label shows A.

Nothing else catches this:
- The busyNow key gate (line 602) is set only by the separate busy() helper (lines 365-368). useLayout only adds the 'busy' CSS class, so keys are not blocked during a layout load.
- loadLayout (lines 71-84) does not use a cached copy of B, because unloadExcept removed B's registry entry and stylesheet links. B's .js and .css really are fetched again asynchronously, so a timing window exists.
- No caller checks whether active matches settings.layout after the load finishes.

Mitigating factors:
- The window is only as long as one local file:// script+CSS load, so it needs a fairly quick Right-then-Left or Right-then-Back.
- The effect is cosmetic: the wrong layout is shown, and nothing is lost or crashes.
- It is easy to recover from. Opening the picker again resets the index from settings.layout, and any further step or OK calls useLayout again. A relaunch also fixes it.

That makes it a real but low-impact race. I am lowering it from P2 to P3. The suggested fix is correct: increment layoutToken before the early return, or track the in-flight id.

UPHELD: I could not refute this. The code does what the claim says. In web/app.mjs:95-103, useLayout returns at `if(active?.id===id)return;` before `++layoutToken`. While layout B is loading, active.id is still A. So useLayout(A) from stepPick(-1) (line 426, reached via keys at 626-627), from endPick(false) on Back/closeAll (lines 254, 262), or from endPick(true) (line 628) leaves the token unchanged, and the pending load of B passes `token===layoutToken` and mounts B. Input is not gated: busyNow, checked at line 602, is only set by busy() and never by useLayout. The race also compounds. With Right,Right,Left,Left the final A is a no-op and B still mounts. The window is realistic on a Fire TV stick: one stylesheet link per sheet plus a script tag from file:// that must download and parse, while users often double-tap arrows. I am lowering the severity to P3. Nothing is lost or corrupted: settings.layout stays correct (A), the wrong layout goes away on the next launch, and the user can fix it at once by opening the picker again and stepping to A, which is no longer the active id once B is mounted. It is a confusing mismatch between the picker label or Settings row and the dashboard, not a broken feature. The suggested fix (bump the token before the early return and clear the busy class) is correct.

confirmed.title: Holding OK on the keyboard's Search key repeats explicit geocoder searches and can auto-accept the first result through the confirm screen
confirmed.trigger: On Settings > Location (or first run), type a street address and press and hold OK on 'Search' a little too long. The remote sends repeated Enter keydowns (e.repeat), and each one reaches select(focused) -> typeKey('search') -> runSearch(true).
confirmed.impact: (1) Each repeat starts a new searchAddress chain: a Census request plus an Open-Meteo time-zone lookup per match, then Nominatim. For non-US homes (skipCensus) every repeat is a Nominatim request. Earlier chains are not cancelled, only ignored through searchSeq. That breaks the 'one request per search' Nominatim policy the code comments promise, and a half-second hold produces 10-20 requests. (2) If the hold lasts until the results arrive, runSearch moves focus to the first result (line 491). The next repeat selects it and opens #confirm with 'Use this' focused, and the following repeat runs choosePlace -> applyPlace(fresh:true). The location is replaced and the 'Recently above' history and logbook are wiped before the user has seen the match. The earlier report covered held OK toggling the picker and edit mode; this path talks to third-party services and commits a destructive location change.
confirmed.evidence: The keydown handler (line 670) is `if(k==='Enter'||k===' '&&layer.id!=='locate'){e.preventDefault();return select(focused);}` with no e.repeat check. typeKey (line 452) has `else if(key==='search')return runSearch(true);`. runSearch has no in-flight guard: `seq=++searchSeq` and the work starts unconditionally. Line 491 is `if(explicit&&layer?.id==='locate')setFocus(box.firstElementChild);`. confirmPlace opens with open('confirm','confirm-ok'), and confirm-ok -> choosePlace -> applyPlace(place,{fresh:true}), which calls store.remove(HISTORY_KEY) and resetLog().
confirmed.fix: Ignore Enter/OK keydowns with e.repeat on every screen, at least on locate, confirm, welcome and the Settings rows. In runSearch, skip an explicit search when the same query is already in flight (keep the in-flight query and promise).
reasons:
UPHELD: Half of the claim holds up and half does not.

What holds (request flood): the keydown handler at web/app.mjs:634 (not line 670) is `if(k==='Enter'||k===' '&&layer.id!=='locate'){...return select(focused);}` and never checks e.repeat. select (line 507) calls typeKey(el.dataset.key), and typeKey('search') at line 452 calls runSearch(true). runSearch (lines 463-492) has no in-flight guard. It bumps searchSeq and immediately calls searchAddress (web/place.mjs:107). confirmed.title: Logbook plane cap evicts all-digit hex aircraft first (integer-like keys), so they delete themselves and inflate the 'Rarest' all-time tally every poll
confirmed.trigger: Once log.planes holds more than 4000 aircraft in a local day (easy at map radius 50-250 mi, where up to 300 aircraft per poll from a feed of up to 250 NM go into log.planes; also possible at busy hubs at smaller radii), any visible aircraft whose ICAO hex is six decimal digits not starting with 0 (for example 406123 or 3c-free European/other blocks, about 10% of random hex codes) is seen on a poll.
confirmed.impact: JS orders integer-like property names ('406123') before string keys, so Object.keys(log.planes)[0] is the smallest all-digit hex, not the oldest entry. When such an aircraft is first recorded, the cap check right after the insert deletes keys[0], which is usually that same aircraft. On the next poll it is missing again, so it is re-created and typesAll[type] is incremented again, then deleted again. Observed with node: 4000 planes already logged, then one Cessna (hex 406123, C172) stays in view for 10 polls while one new plane arrives per poll. typesAll.C172 went 0 to 10 and the plane was never kept in log.planes. Expected: a tally of 1 and the plane kept. Over hours the all-time type tallies for those aircraft's types grow by one per poll (every 5-15 s). That corrupts 'Rarest' permanently, because typesAll is carried over every day and saved to localStorage. Those aircraft are also left out of Rarest and Farthest for the rest of the day, because their records (closest distance, origin) are thrown away.
confirmed.evidence: model.mjs:96-99: `rec=log.planes[a.hex]={d}; if(a.aircraft_type)log.typesAll[...]++; const keys=Object.keys(log.planes);if(keys.length>4000)delete log.planes[keys[0]];` log.planes is a plain object keyed by hex. Reproduced with node importing web/model.mjs updateLog: after the 10 polls, typesAll.C172 was 10, log.planes['406123'] was missing, and pickRarest skipped the aircraft.
confirmed.fix: Evict by insertion time, not by key order. Store log.planes as an array of [hex, rec] or keep a separate insertion-ordered list of hexes (log.order), and evict the first entry of that. Alternatively, prefix keys (for example 'h'+hex) so none is integer-like, migrating old logs. Never evict the record that was just inserted. Also consider keeping a per-day set of tallied hexes separate from log.planes, so an evicted plane is not tallied again in typesAll.
reasons:
UPHELD: I could not refute it. The defect is real and reproduces. At web/model.mjs:94-99, updateLog creates rec=log.planes[a.hex], increments typesAll, then runs `delete log.planes[Object.keys(log.planes)[0]]` once there are more than 4000 keys. The call path is live: liveSource (model.mjs:213-218) passes up to MAX_PLANES=300 enriched aircraft from the whole feed into updateLog on every fresh poll. LOG_MILES only gates Seen/Highest/Fastest/Cargo, after the insert and eviction. Keys are lowercased hex strings (line 210). In JS, a canonical integer key such as '406123' is enumerated before every string key, in ascending order. So keys[0] is the smallest all-digit hex, not the oldest entry. Hexes with a leading 0 (e.g. '0d1234') are not canonical integers, so they are not affected.

I reproduced it with node. I seeded 4000 'a…' planes, then ran 10 polls, each with hex 406123 (C172) plus one new plane. Result: typesAll.C172 = 10, '406123' was absent from log.planes, there were 4000 keys, and pickRarest(log,10) returned null.

Caveat on reach: the home is in the US (Census geocoding), and US registrations ('a…') and Canadian ones ('c…') are never all-digit. So the affected aircraft are mainly foreign international flights: UK 40-43, Germany 3c, France 38-3b, Netherlands 48, UAE 89, China 78, Australia 7c. That is fewer than the claim's "about 10% of random hex codes", but these aircraft are common near large international hubs. The bug also needs more than 4000 unique aircraft in one local day. That is plausible at large map radii near a busy region (300 nearest of a 250 NM feed every 5-15 s), but not at a typical small radius. Once triggered, the inflation persists, because typesAll carries over between days and is saved to localStorage. It also affects other all-digit planes still in view, not only the newly inserted one: when one is evicted it is re-created and tallied again on the next poll. The suggested fix is sound: evict by insertion order (a separate order array or a 'h'-prefixed key), and never evict the record just inserted. P2 is defensible given the permanent corruption, though the reach is conditional.

UPHELD: I could not refute the mechanism. It is real and I reproduced it.

**Code:** at web/model.mjs:96-99, a new hex is inserted into the plain object log.planes. The cap check then runs `Object.keys(log.planes)` and deletes `keys[0]`.

**Hex format:** web/live.mjs:84/127 confirms hexes are 6-char hex strings (validated with HEX and lowercased). An all-digit hex with no leading zero, such as '406123', is a canonical array index, so JS lists it before all string keys in ascending numeric order. `keys[0]` is therefore the smallest all-digit hex, not the oldest entry. This holds for the whole ranges 300000-39FFFF (Italy, Spain, France) and 400000-43FFFF (UK), plus the all-digit codes in other blocks.

**Reproduction:** I ran node importing web/model.mjs with 4000 planes already logged. A plane with hex 406123 (type C172) stayed in view for 10 polls while one new plane arrived per poll. Result: typesAll.C172 was 10, '406123' was not in log.planes, and the size stayed at 4000. This matches the claim. Each re-insert re-tallies typesAll, and app.mjs:218 saves the result to localStorage (store.set) on every fresh poll. Because typesAll carries over between days, the inflation is permanent.

**Why the severity drops for a TV user:**
- The 4000-per-local-day cap is only reachable at wide map radii in busy airspace. The feed is ~1.5x the map radius, capped at 250 NM (app.mjs:30-38, MAP_RADII up to 250). Smaller radii or quiet areas never hit it.
- For US viewers, US-registered hexes start with 'a' and are not affected. Only foreign aircraft are hit (UK, France, Italy, Spain and so on), which are often long-haul widebodies.
- The only harm is to a cosmetic logbook stat. The affected types stop showing as 'Rarest', and those aircraft drop out of Rarest and Farthest for the rest of that day.
- There is no crash, no loss of the live display and no growth in storage, since typesAll holds only integer counts.

So the defect is real and the claim is correct. Given that it needs non-default wide radii and only affects one stat, P3 fits better than P2. Suggested fix stands: evict by insertion order (a separate order list, or 'h'-prefixed keys), never evict the record just inserted, and track tallied hexes per day separately from log.planes.

confirmed.title: Saving Adjust position does not redraw the street map in detail layouts, so the map stays offset by the adjustment
confirmed.trigger: Use a detail-map layout (Atlas Dark, the default, or Atlas Light, Atlas Satellite, Glass, Blueprint or Sectional) after its street map has loaded. Open Adjust position, move the dot by roughly 120 m to 1 km, and press OK. choosePlace treats any move over 0.001 degrees as changed and calls applyPlace(place,{fresh:true}). Because the move is under 0.01 degrees, same(maps.base), maps.base.range===range, same(maps.detail) and detailFits are all true, so keepBase and keepDetail are both true.
confirmed.impact: applyPlace skips mapsChanged() (line 178) and choosePlace skips refreshLayout(), so nothing repaints the layout's map. Every canvas and label was painted with mapShift() relative to the old S.place, but the new feed places aircraft relative to the new HOME. The streets, place and airport labels, Atlas Satellite imagery (positioned from place in drawSatellite) and the Sectional graticule (drawn from ctx.place()) all stay drawn for the old point while the home marker and planes use the new one. The map therefore ends up offset by exactly the correction the user just made, about 40 px for a 300 m move at a 2-mile radius. This lasts until a layout switch, a radius change or a relaunch. Layouts with only a base map are not affected, because maps.detail is null for them, so keepDetail is false and mapsChanged() runs.

confirmed.fix: In applyPlace, call mapsChanged() whenever the place differs from the one the layout last painted for, even when the maps are kept. For example, change line 178 to `mapsChanged();` unconditionally, or call mapsChanged() from choosePlace after applyPlace.

The map stays offset by the correction until something calls setMap or refresh, such as a layout switch or a radius change. confirmed.title: A Planespotters image that fails to load leaves an empty photo frame with the credit and QR code, and the bundled model photo is never tried
confirmed.trigger: photoFor returns a valid record (the API JSON came through), but the CDN image itself fails to load. Examples: the photo was removed, the CDN returns 403/404, or a network blip. The image is loaded directly by the WebView from p.src.
confirmed.impact: showPhotoIn sets s.hidden=false and the src, but registers only onload. With no onerror handler, the slot stays visible with an empty 58 px-high image box, a QR code and '© <photographer> · Planespotters.net' crediting a photo that is not shown. The modelPhoto(a) fallback is not used, and layouts that hide their legend for the photo (Sectional swaps out the Legend box, Glass and Blueprint show the photo card) keep the empty card for as long as that aircraft is the hero. Atlas's own copy has the same gap (atlas.mjs:225).
confirmed.evidence: kit.mjs:46 `if(p&&qr){s._img.src=p.src;s._qr.src=qr;...}`, then line 53 `s.hidden=false`, and line 55 sets only `s._img.onload=fit`. A grep for onerror in web/*.mjs and web/layouts/*.mjs finds only the stylesheet and script loaders in app.mjs. whatsup.css:134 gives .ph-img a fixed 58 px height.
confirmed.fix: Add `s._img.onerror=()=>{if(s._hex!==hex)return; const m=modelPhoto(a); if(m){/* switch to the model branch */}else{s.hidden=true;s._qr.removeAttribute('src');} relayout();}`. Do the same in atlas.mjs showPhoto, clearing `photo` so render hides $.pic.

It assigns only `s._img.onload=fit` (line 55). No onerror is registered. A grep of web/*.mjs and web/layouts/*.mjs finds onerror only in the app.mjs stylesheet and script loaders.
- **Nothing checks the image before it is shown.** photoFor (web/photos.mjs:29-44) only fetches the API JSON through the bridge. parsePhoto checks the URL shape with a regex and never loads the image. confirmed.title: Sectional graticule leaves out the meridians near the chart's left and right edges at high latitudes
confirmed.trigger: Sectional layout with home above about 57 degrees latitude (Scotland, Scandinavia, Alaska, Iceland) at the default 10-mile radius, or similar settings. The meridian loop runs only over `lon0±span*1.5` with `span=max(.2,range()/69*1.6)` degrees, a span that ignores cos(latitude). The chart's half-width in longitude, about 330/(69.172*cos(lat)*PPM), grows quickly toward the poles.
confirmed.impact: At latitude 70 and 10 mi, meridians stop at ±0.348 degrees while the chart reaches about ±0.55 degrees. That leaves a band about 120 px wide on each side with no longitude lines or edge labels, about two 5-minute meridians per side. At latitude 65 about one meridian per side is missing. The latitude lines still cross the full width, so the graticule looks cut off.
confirmed.evidence: sectional.mjs:90 `span=Math.max(.2,range()/69*1.6)`. Line 96 `for(let lo=Math.ceil((lon0-span*1.5)/step)*step;lo<lon0+span*1.5;lo+=step)`. x is computed as `CX+(lo-lon0)*69.172*cos*PPM` and dropped only if outside 8..W-8. Example at lat 70: px/deg = 69.172*0.342*25.5 ≈ 603, so the right edge at x=672 is (672-345)/603 ≈ 0.54 degrees, beyond 0.348.
confirmed.fix: Derive the longitude span from the chart width, for example `const lonSpan=Math.max(CX,W-CX)/(69.172*cos*PPM)+step;`, and loop over `lon0±lonSpan`. The existing x<8 / x>W-8 test then trims the meridians off the chart.

The meridian loop at line 96 therefore covers only ±range*0.0348 degrees. The chart's right half-width in longitude is (W-CX)/(69.172*cos*PPM), which equals range*0.0190/cos degrees. Above the minimum span, the range cancels out: meridians are missing whenever cos(lat) < 0.546, so above about 57 degrees, at any radius. At lat 70 and 10 mi, the step is 5' because 5*69/60*25.5 = 147 >= 70. The loop stops at ±0.348 degrees while the chart reaches about ±0.555 degrees, so roughly two 5' meridians per side are never drawn, along with their labels. The only filter on meridians is x<8 or x>W-8 at line 97, so nothing else draws them. The latitude lines at lines 92-94 still cross the full width. The effect is cosmetic and appears only at high latitudes, so P3 stands. The suggested fix, deriving the longitude span from max(CX, W-CX)/(69.172*cos*PPM), is correct.

confirmed.trigger: Start at the default 10-mile radius with a detail layout (Atlas, Glass, Blueprint or Sectional), wait for the street map, press Up to 15 mi (or 25+), let that map build, then press Down back to 10 mi. Relaunching the app at 10 mi after visiting another radius ≥10 does the same.

The app rebuilds about 32-50 vector tiles (z11 main roads plus the z12 inner side streets), writes about 2 MB to localStorage again, and the screen shows 'Drawing the street map…' with no detail in the meantime. Every round trip pays this cost twice. In buildMap (web/mapgen.mjs:129), range<=10 gives lim = 3 mi. eachTile only fetches tiles inside ±lim around the original point (mapgen.mjs:86-91), and clipLine/touches drop anything outside that ±3 mi box. nudge() (app.mjs:583-589) only changes adj.latitude/longitude and has no bound on movement. drawAdjust paints adj.map with center:c, so paintMap/mapShift (kit.mjs:248) shift the old geometry. Nothing rebuilds the map: the async rebuild only runs in startAdjust and is keyed to adj.place, which never changes while nudging. Once the 1 mi view circle passes the 3 mi box edge it goes blank.

This is realistic on a TV. The ZIP/city confirm text (app.mjs:207) tells users to move the dot from a centroid, and suburban or rural ZIP centroids are often 2-5 mi from a home. A held arrow moves up to 400 m per repeat, so about 3 mi takes only a few seconds of holding.

There is a non-obvious workaround. The user can save part way, then reopen Adjust position from Settings ('set-adjust' calls startAdjust(settings.place), which rebuilds the map around the saved point). Nothing tells the user to do this, and the screen just shows no streets, so it is still a real UX defect. It is limited to setup, so P3 is right.

confirmed.title: The page is never told when the app goes to the background, so feed polling, lookups and storage writes keep running behind other apps
confirmed.trigger: Open What's Up, then press Home or switch to another app (Netflix, Prime Video). Vega keeps the singleton app resident, and the WebView with its timers stays alive.
confirmed.impact: Observed: the AppState listener (App.tsx:134-138) only turns the engagement report and the silent loop on or off. Nothing reaches the WebView, and the web code has no visibilitychange or hidden check. So the feed loop (web/live.mjs:312-327) keeps calling adsb.fi every pollSeconds (5-15 s, app.mjs:38) through the native bridge for as long as the app is backgrounded, which can be hours. It also keeps fetching adsb.lol routes and Planespotters photos, keeps rewriting whatsup.history.v1 in localStorage on every poll that has a plane inside, and keeps running chime gating. The host already expects this traffic: App.tsx:183 drops 'chime' requests that arrive in the background, which can only happen if the page is still polling there. Expected: a backgrounded TV app stops its network polling, since it costs the user's bandwidth, the stick's CPU while they watch something else, and adsb.fi request volume that the back-off issue already flags.
confirmed.evidence: src/App.tsx:134-138: `AppState.addEventListener('change', state => { active = state === 'active'; engage(active); setActive(active); })`. No injectJavaScript call here. src/App.tsx:182-186: chime requests are checked against AppState.currentState !== 'background'. grep finds no 'visibilitychange'/'document.hidden' in web/*.mjs. web/live.mjs:327: `timer=setTimeout(poll,Math.max(1000,config.pollSeconds*1000-...))` with no pause condition.
confirmed.fix: In the AppState handler, inject `window.__whatsupActive&&window.__whatsupActive(${active});true;`. In web/app.mjs, define __whatsupActive so that false calls feed?.stop() and pauses map-build retries, and true calls restartFeed(), which re-polls at once so the data is fresh on return. Also have the bridge's onMessage refuse 'get' requests while AppState is 'background', so that any leftover timers send nothing.
reasons: UPHELD: Not refuted on the code, but how much it matters on a real device is unproven. Every code claim checks out. The AppState handler at src/App.tsx:134-138 only calls engage() and setActive(). The only injectJavaScript calls go to __whatsupBack (Back key) and __whatsupReply (bridge replies), so the page is never told the app went to the background. The web code never checks visibilitychange, document.hidden, pagehide or focus/blur. poll() at web/live.mjs:312-327 reschedules itself with setTimeout and stops only on the stopped flag. On every poll that has a plane inside, it rewrites HISTORY_KEY (live.mjs:320) and calls enrich() (live.mjs:325). onMessage (App.tsx:174-224) answers 'get' requests in any app state. The chime guard at App.tsx:183 shows the author expected page messages to arrive while the app is backgrounded. So nothing in the app's own code stops polling. What I could not confirm from the repo is whether Vega actually keeps a backgrounded app's WebView JS timers running, or instead suspends or kills them. Nothing in the repo shows background behaviour on a device: TESTING.md:82 covers only the engagement report, which is a jest unit test. If Vega freezes background apps, the real effect is small. Because of that, and because there is no proof on a device, I'm lowering it from P2 to P3. The suggested fix is still correct and cheap: inject __whatsupActive(false/true) from the AppState handler, have it call feed.stop() / restartFeed(), and refuse 'get' requests in onMessage while AppState is 'background'.

UPHELD: The code-level claim checks out. The AppState handler in src/App.tsx:134-138 only calls engage(active) and setActive(active), and setActive only drives the silent loop (lines 146-152). Nothing sends a message to the WebView: the only injectJavaScript calls are for Back (line 167) and the bridge replies (lines 206 and 217). In web/*.mjs there is no visibilitychange, document.hidden or pause hook. The feed loop in web/live.mjs:312-327 stops only when stopped is set by stop(), and it re-arms with setTimeout every pollSeconds. On every successful poll with planes inside it calls store.set(HISTORY_KEY) and enrich(). The onMessage bridge serves 'get' requests no matter what AppState is; only 'chime' is gated, at line 183. That gate shows the author expected the page to keep running in the background. No guard elsewhere handles this.

One thing the code cannot prove is the runtime effect. If Vega suspends the backgrounded app process, or the WebView throttles timers, the polling stops on its own. TESTING.md and the tests only cover keep-awake engagement, so this is unverified. The cost is also small: a few KB per adsb.fi poll and some routes/photos lookups, on mains-powered hardware, with no visible error. I'm treating it as a real gap but downgrading it from P2 to P3.

The suggested fix fits the code: inject a __whatsupActive(bool) call from the AppState handler. On false, call feed.stop(); on true, call restartFeed(). As a backstop, have onMessage drop 'get' requests while AppState.currentState === 'background'.

UPHELD: The code facts hold up. src/App.tsx:134-138 only toggles engage() and the silent loop's `active` state. Nothing is injected into the WebView on an AppState change. The only injectJavaScript calls are for Back (line 167) and bridge replies (lines 206/217). There is no visibilitychange or document.hidden handling under web/ or src/. The poll() loop in web/live.mjs:312-327 reschedules itself with setTimeout and has no pause condition, and the 'get' bridge in onMessage has no background check. The manifest uses launch-type = "singleton", and the chime guard at App.tsx:183 shows the author expects the page to keep sending messages while backgrounded. So the defect is real in code.

The severity is overstated, though. Nothing goes wrong for the user. Data is fresh again on the next poll after they return, and nothing they can see breaks. The cost is one small adsb.fi JSON request every 5-15 s, plus occasional route and photo lookups for new aircraft, which are cached or deduped by the enricher. On a home connection that is negligible. CPU use on the stick is small next to a video app running in the foreground.

It is also unconfirmed that timers keep running at full rate on the device. Vega may suspend or kill backgrounded apps under memory pressure. If the Chromium-based WebView marks the page hidden, chained timers are throttled, and after about 5 minutes hidden that drops to roughly once per minute. TESTING.md has no on-device check of background traffic. The fix the claim suggests (inject __whatsupActive(false/true) from the AppState handler and gate 'get' requests in the background) is reasonable hygiene and cheap to add, but this is a P3 efficiency issue, not a P2 defect.

confirmed.title: One adsb.fi entry with an object-valued field stops the feed poll loop for good (until relaunch)
confirmed.trigger: The adsb.fi payload has any entry whose `hex` is a JSON object with a non-callable `toString`, e.g. {"hex":{"toString":0}}. A valid entry whose `emergency` (line 170) or `year` (line 178) is such an object does the same. JSON.parse builds an own `toString` property, so `String(r.hex)` / `String(r.emergency)` / `String(r.year)` throw 'Cannot convert object to primitive value'.
confirmed.impact: liveSource's onUpdate callback throws. poll() calls it at web/live.mjs:324 outside any try, so the async poll rejects before reaching `timer=setTimeout(poll,...)` (live.mjs:327). No more polls are scheduled. The dashboard freezes on the last model with no 'connecting'/stale state, and no new model is ever produced, until the app is relaunched or a setting restarts the feed. Expected: the bad entry is skipped (the line-210 comment says 'one bad entry must not drop the update') and polling continues. The earlier null-entry fix (filter r&&typeof r==='object') does not cover this because the entry is an object.
confirmed.evidence: Ran a node harness (scratchpad feedkill.mjs) that calls model.start() with a stubbed fetch. With only a valid entry: 6 feed fetches and 11 models in 5 s. With an extra entry {hex:{toString:0}}, or a valid entry carrying emergency:{toString:0}: 1 fetch, 1 model, then 'unhandledRejection: Cannot convert object to primitive value' and no further polls.
confirmed.fix: Put the body of poll() after the fetch in try/finally, so `timer=setTimeout(poll,...)` always runs and a throwing onUpdate cannot end the loop. Separately, stop calling String() on raw feed values: use typeof checks (`typeof r.hex==='string'`, `typeof r.emergency==='string'`, `typeof r.year==='string'||typeof r.year==='number'`) at model.mjs:170, 178 and 210.
reasons: UPHELD: The code path is real and reproduces, but I'm downgrading it to P3 because it needs a malformed feed. At web/model.mjs:210 the guard `.filter(r=>r&&typeof r==='object')` lets through any object entry, and then `String(r.hex)` runs on every entry. `String(JSON.parse('{"toString":0}'))` throws 'Cannot convert object to primitive value' (checked with node -e). The same applies to `String(r.emergency)` at line 170 (`{toString:0}` passes the `r.emergency&&r.emergency!=='none'` check) and `String(r.year)` at line 178. That onModel callback is the onUpdate that startLive gets (live.mjs:272). In poll() (live.mjs:310-328), `onUpdate(states,true)` at line 324 is not inside any try. The throw therefore rejects the async poll before `timer=setTimeout(poll,...)` at line 327, and nothing in web/*.mjs catches unhandled rejections or reschedules the poll. So the loop does stop for good, as claimed. The claim overstates how likely this is. It needs adsb.fi to send an entry whose hex, emergency or year is a JSON object, which a real ADS-B feed doesn't do (those fields are strings or numbers). Normal data (null entries, missing or non-string fields) doesn't trigger it. It is a real robustness gap: the one-bad-entry guard is incomplete, and there is no try/finally around the reschedule. But it is not a likely ship blocker. The suggested fixes are sound: wrap the poll body in try/finally so setTimeout always runs, and use typeof checks instead of String() on raw feed values.

UPHELD: The mechanism is real and I reproduced it. Running the scratchpad harness gives these results. With only a valid entry: 6 feed fetches and 11 models in 5 s. With an entry {hex:{toString:0}}: 1 fetch, 1 model, then an unhandledRejection 'Cannot convert object to primitive value' and no more polls. With a valid entry carrying emergency:{toString:0}: the same result.

Nothing catches the throw. In web/live.mjs poll(), selection() at line 318 and onUpdate(states,true) at line 324 both run outside any try. If either throws, the async poll rejects before `timer=setTimeout(poll,...)` (line 327), so no further poll is scheduled. Only enrich() has a try/catch. The page has no global unhandledrejection or watchdog handler. The only things that restart the feed are restartFeed() in app.mjs and a settings change.

Two corrections to the claim:
- For a bad `hex`, the first throw is earlier than model.mjs:210. It happens at web/live.mjs:127 (`String(a.hex??'')` in selection), which also runs before the setTimeout. So a typeof guard at model.mjs:210 alone would not fix the hex case. The `emergency` case does reach model.mjs:170 through onUpdate.
- The trigger is contrived. adsb.fi does not send object-valued hex, emergency or year fields with an own non-callable toString, so this only happens with a corrupted or hostile upstream.

The real weakness is that any throw anywhere in the poll body permanently ends the loop with no stale indicator. The fix is still right: wrap poll's body in try/finally so the setTimeout always runs, and use typeof checks instead of String() on raw feed values at live.mjs:127, model.mjs:170, 178 and 210. Because the trigger is unrealistic, I am downgrading the severity from P1.

REFUTED: The code path does exist, but the trigger is not realistic and does not justify P1. In web/live.mjs:315-327, poll() calls onUpdate(states,true) at line 324 with no try/finally, and model.mjs:170, 178 and 210 call String() on raw feed values. So an entry whose JSON object has its own non-callable toString would throw and stop polling.

However, nothing realistic produces that input. adsb.fi serves readsb-format JSON where hex, emergency and year are always strings or numbers, or are missing. An ordinary object such as {"hex":{}} does not throw: String({}) gives "[object Object]", which is then simply never matched. Only a payload with a literal "toString" key set to a non-function value throws, and only a malicious or compromised feed would send that. A compromised feed could already make the app useless just by sending ac:[] or junk data, so this adds little real attack surface. Entries also go through a single WebView JSON.parse, and selection() at live.mjs:84 already rejects non-string hex for the hero/inside path. The crash comes only from the unrestricted String() mapping at model.mjs:210.

There is also partial recovery. restartFeed (app.mjs:163) runs on any settings change, and a relaunch fixes it. For a TV user this would essentially never happen in the field.

What remains is a hardening issue: poll() should put its scheduling in finally, so that any future exception inside onUpdate (from any cause) cannot silently end the loop. The typeof checks are also cheap. That is defensive robustness worth P3, not a P1 ship blocker.

confirmed.title: An object-valued registration in the feed is saved to 'Recently above' history and breaks route lookups for up to 6 h, across relaunches
confirmed.trigger: An adsb.fi entry inside the alert zone has `r` set to an object with a non-callable toString, e.g. "r":{"toString":0}. selection() copies `registration:a.r??''` unvalidated (live.mjs:92). mergeHistory() keeps it, and store.set(HISTORY_KEY) saves it to localStorage. On every later poll, observations() puts history rows from the last 6 h back into the Enricher input. provider() then calls ident(a.registration), and String(obj) throws.
confirmed.impact: Enricher.tick() throws on every poll (caught silently by enrich's try/catch). No ADSB.lol route is looked up or published for any aircraft, so origin/destination, progress bars and 'Farthest' stay blank. This lasts until the poisoned row is older than 6 h or pushed out by 20 newer sightings. It also survives an app restart because the row lives in localStorage. Expected: a malformed registration is dropped and routes keep working.
confirmed.evidence: node test: mergeHistory([], [{hex:'a1b2c3',registration:{toString:0},...}]) after a JSON round-trip persists {"registration":{"toString":0}}. Passing that history to observations() and then Enricher.tick() rejects with 'Cannot convert object to primitive value'.
confirmed.fix: Sanitise at ingestion: in selection() set `registration: typeof a.r==='string'?a.r.trim().slice(0,12):''` and `aircraft_type: typeof a.t==='string'?a.t.slice(0,8):''`. In mergeHistory() and observations(), keep only string callsign/registration fields from saved rows. Making ident() typeof-safe (`typeof v==='string'||typeof v==='number'?String(v):''`) also closes this path.
reasons:
UPHELD: The defect is real, but the trigger is very unlikely, so I'm lowering it from P2 to P3.

**The code path reproduces.** Line 88 of web/live.mjs (the cited line 92 is close) copies `registration:a.r??''` without checking its type. mergeHistory (lines 98-105) keeps it, and line 320 saves it to localStorage. `startLive` reloads that history on every launch. On each poll, `observations()` (lines 122-123) puts rows from the last 6 h back in unfiltered. `Enricher.tick` then calls `provider(a)` on each row, which calls `ident(a.registration)` (line 112). I ran `ident()` on `JSON.parse('{"r":{"toString":0}}').r` and it throws "Cannot convert object to primitive value". The `try/catch` in `enrich()` (lines 293-301) swallows the error, so the route ledger stops updating for every aircraft. The row stays until it is older than 6 h or pushed out by 20 newer sightings, and it survives a relaunch.

**The impact is a little wider than claimed.** While the plane is still in the feed, line 130 calls `ident(a.r)` on the raw entry and throws there too.

**Why P3.** Only an object that shadows `toString`/`valueOf` with something not callable throws. A plain object such as `{a:1}` just becomes "[object Object]", which `ident` rejects without error. So it needs adsb.fi to send a malformed or hostile `r` value. It is a trusted-feed hardening issue, not a likely failure in the field, and the app recovers on its own.

**Fix.** The suggested ones work. Type-check `r`/`t` in `selection()`, or make `ident()` accept only strings and numbers. The `ident()` change also covers line 130.

UPHELD: I could not refute the mechanism, and I reproduced it. selection() in web/live.mjs:88 copies `registration:a.r??''` without checking its type. mergeHistory() (lines 98-104) only validates hex and last_seen, so the object is saved under HISTORY_KEY and comes back after a JSON round-trip. observations() (lines 122-123) puts history rows from the last 6 h back into the list with their fields spread unchanged. Enricher.tick() then calls provider(a), and ident(a.registration) runs String({toString:0}) at line 110, which throws. My node run printed 'ERR Cannot convert object to primitive value'. Nothing catches it per aircraft. enrich()'s try/catch (lines 293-301) swallows the error for the whole tick, so no route is looked up or published on any poll while the row is in history, including after a restart. The same throw also happens on the live path at line 130 (ident(a.r)).

I am downgrading it because the trigger is unlikely. Ordinary malformed values do not break anything: a number, null, or a plain object like {"a":1} becomes "[object Object]", which ident rejects quietly. The throw only happens when the object has a non-callable toString or valueOf key. adsb.fi does not send that in normal operation, so it would take a deliberately crafted or corrupted upstream payload. The impact is also limited: route enrichment stops for at most 6 h or 20 newer sightings, and nothing crashes. The suggested fix is still correct and cheap: make ident() check the type, or keep only string fields in selection() and mergeHistory().

REFUTED: The code path is real, but it should not be rated P2. Confirmed by reading the code: selection() at web/live.mjs:88 copies `registration: a.r ?? ''` without checking its type. mergeHistory() at lines 98-105 keeps it, and poll() at line 320 saves it to localStorage. observations() at lines 119-123 puts history rows from the last 6 h back into the enricher input, carrying the raw registration. provider() at line 112 then calls ident(), and ident() at line 110 runs String(v||''). For an object whose toString is not callable, that throws a TypeError. enrich() at lines 292-301 catches the error silently, so routes stop updating.

Why the claimed impact and severity are not realistic for a TV user:
(1) The trigger requires adsb.fi to send `r` as a JSON object containing a "toString" key set to a non-function. The real feed sends `r` as a string or leaves it out. A plain object such as {} or {"x":1} does not throw: it becomes "[object Object]", fails ident's regex and returns ''. Only an object built specifically to break this triggers it. That means a compromised or hostile upstream, not normal bad data.
(2) An upstream that hostile has much worse options than making route lookups fail quietly. The same live record already breaks routes on that poll through ident(a.r) in observations() at line 130.
(3) The damage is limited and the app degrades gracefully. The plane list, map, photos and alerts keep running. Only origin/destination enrichment pauses, and it recovers on its own within 6 h or after 20 newer sightings.

This is worth fixing as cheap hardening. Make ident() type-safe (`typeof v==='string'?v:''`), or check that `r` and `t` are strings in selection(). It is a P3 robustness issue, not a P2 that ships to users.

confirmed.title: A stopped feed's in-flight route lookup still renders and saves: old place/zone model drawn after a restart, new ledger/logbook overwritten
confirmed.trigger: A feed restart while an ADSB.lol route request is in flight. A restart happens when the location changes (applyPlace, app.mjs:164), the alert zone or radius is edited (restartFeed, app.mjs:160), or the map radius is stepped. enrich() is not awaited by poll(). Its getJson(ROUTE_URL) can take up to 8 s plus a 2 s page timer on a slow network, so the window is wide when the network is degraded. Even on a healthy network it is hit regularly, because a lookup runs every 5 s while routes are missing.
confirmed.impact: stop() only sets `stopped`. poll() and checkCoverage check that flag, but enrich() (live.mjs:282-292) does not. When the late reply arrives, the dead feed calls onUpdate(states,true), which runs liveSource's callback and then app render(). That sets lastModel, runs the chime gate and draws the OLD feed's planes, hero and inside flags under the OLD alert zone or radius. model.start() has already replaced the global HOME, so the old aircraft are also positioned against the new home. This is the next frame after the user changes location or zone, until the new feed's next poll up to 5-15 s later. On the same reply the dead feed writes its own Ledger to LEDGER_KEY (live.mjs:289), overwriting lookups the new feed has saved; those are re-requested from adsb.lol. Its liveSource also writes its in-memory logbook to LOG_KEY (model.mjs:203). After a location change with fresh:true, that brings back the old place's 'Today' logbook that applyPlace had just cleared with resetLog(). The new feed overwrites it only on its next fresh update; if that update never comes (new feed failing) or the app is closed first, the old place's counts stay for the new place.
confirmed.evidence: Reproduced with node and a mocked fetch: startLive with one UAL123 aircraft; the adsb.lol fetch is delayed 1.5 s; feed.stop() is called at 500 ms. Output: 'stopped' then 'onUpdate AFTER stop, ok= true' and 'updates after stop: 1'. Code: enrich() { ... routes=await enricher.tick(...); states={...}; if(ledger.dirty){...store.set(LEDGER_KEY,ledger);} onUpdate(states,true); } has no `if(stopped)return` after the await, unlike poll() (live.mjs:310, 318).
confirmed.fix: In enrich(), after `await enricher.tick(...)`, add `if(stopped)return;` before touching `states`, the store or onUpdate. Optionally pass an AbortSignal or token into Enricher.tick so a stopped feed also skips the ledger.put calls.
reasons: UPHELD: The code path is real. In web/live.mjs:282-292, enrich() awaits enricher.tick() and then runs states=..., store.set(LEDGER_KEY,ledger) and onUpdate(states,true) without checking `stopped`. stop() (live.mjs:323) only sets the flag and clears the timer. poll() calls enrich() without awaiting it (live.mjs:316). Nothing downstream guards against a stale feed. liveSource's callback (model.mjs:203-223) calls updateLog/store.set(LOG_KEY) when `fresh`, then calls onModel. app.mjs passes `render` directly to start(), and model.start() (model.mjs:296) has no generation token. The placeToken only gates startFeed, not render. So a late route reply after restartFeed or applyPlace (app.mjs:163-171) sets lastModel, runs listen() and draws the old feed's planes. The old aircraft carry `inside` computed against the old config, and their positions are computed against the new HOME. listen() also runs with chime=null, so a spurious chime is possible. The logbook claim also holds: the old closure's in-memory `log` is written back to LOG_KEY after resetLog(). However, the new feed loaded its log from the store at its own start, after the reset, so its in-memory log stays clean. Its next fresh update overwrites the stale value, which means the persistent effect needs the new feed to never get a fresh update. Overall the defect is real, but the impact is mostly a transient wrong frame (until the next poll, about 5 s), a possible stray chime, and some redundant adsb.lol re-lookups. That fits P3 better than P2. Fix as suggested: add `if(stopped)return;` right after the await in enrich().

UPHELD: The defect is real. In web/live.mjs:282-292, enrich() awaits enricher.tick() and then calls store.set(LEDGER_KEY) and onUpdate(states,true). Nothing checks `stopped` after the await. stop() (live.mjs:323) only sets the flag and clears the poll timer. None of the callers catch this. restartFeed and applyPlace (app.mjs:163-181) call feed.stop() and then start a new feed. They pass the same `render` callback, and render (app.mjs:160) has no feed-identity or token check. The placeToken check in applyPlace only gates map building and startFeed, not render. liveSource (model.mjs:203-221) calls onModel without condition, and when fresh it writes its in-memory `log` to LOG_KEY (model.mjs:218). That log was loaded before resetLog(), so a late reply can bring back the old place's log. model.start() has already replaced HOME/TZ and cleared samples, so the old feed's planes are drawn against the new home with the old config's inAlert zone. render clears chime to null on restart and then calls listen(), so the stale model can also ring a false chime. The damage is mostly temporary: the next fresh update from the new feed redraws the screen and rewrites the log, and the overwritten ledger only loses lookups made since the restart, which are fetched again. The lasting log effect needs the new feed to never update or the app to close first. Even so, the stale frame, the possible false chime and the stale writes are concrete and reachable. Fix: add `if(stopped)return;` right after the await in enrich().

UPHELD: The mechanism is real, but P2 overstates what a TV user would see.

Confirmed:
- enrich() in web/live.mjs:282-292 never checks `stopped` after `await enricher.tick(...)`.
- stop() in live.mjs:334 only sets the flag and clears the poll timer.
- So a late adsb.lol reply makes the dead feed write LEDGER_KEY and call onUpdate(states,true).
- That runs the old liveSource and then app render(). render() sets lastModel, runs listen() and draws, using the old feed's planes, zone and inside flags, and the new global HOME that start() has already set.
- The old liveSource also writes its in-memory log to LOG_KEY (model.mjs:218). Its `log` was loaded before resetLog() ran in applyPlace (app.mjs:171).

Why the impact is small:
(1) The stale picture is short-lived. A restart only comes from a user action in Settings (location, zone or radius change; app.mjs:163-191, 346, 360, 391). The new feed calls poll() right away (live.mjs:333). Its first good reply, normally under a second and at most 4 s, replaces lastModel with a correct model. On a healthy network the old feed's adsb.lol reply also usually arrives in well under a second, so the two must overlap closely for the glitch to happen at all. The claimed "5-15 s" only applies when the network is degraded.
(2) No false chime. Restarts set chime=null, and chimeGate (core.mjs:192) returns ring:false on the first ready frame. The stale frame can only seed the chime state with the old count, which at worst delays a later chime by the 60 s quiet window.
(3) The ledger overwrite costs little. Route cache entries are keyed by callsign, not by place. The old ledger is a near-superset of what the new feed loaded at start. The only loss is the one or two lookups the new feed made in the last few seconds, which are simply fetched again within the 5 s cooldown.
(4) The logbook is only contaminated in edge cases. The new liveSource read LOG_KEY at start, when it was already empty, and keeps its own copy in memory. Its next fresh update (normally within one poll) overwrites the stale LOG_KEY. The old place's counts only stay if the app is closed in that short window, or if the new feed never gets a fresh update.

Conclusion: this is a real race worth the one-line fix (`if(stopped)return;` right after the await in enrich()). The user-visible effect is a rare, brief wrong frame after a Settings change, plus a narrow edge case for the logbook. That is P3, not P2.

confirmed.title: Receiver-coverage probe downloads the full 250 NM adsb.fi area whenever the local sky is empty, and every feed restart repeats it
confirmed.trigger: Any period with an empty feed at the user's radius, for example at night with the default 10 mi map (15 NM feed). The empty feed calls checkCoverage(), which asks for FEED_URL(...,MAX_NM=250). `coverage={none:false,checked:0}` is created per startLive, so each restartFeed/applyPlace runs the probe again at once. confirmed.title: store.get returns the stale localStorage copy after a failed store.set, so restarts roll the logbook, Recently-above history and route ledger back
confirmed.trigger: localStorage is near quota (base maps, two detail slots and a growing logbook live in the same origin), so a store.set(LOG_KEY / HISTORY_KEY / LEDGER_KEY) throws QuotaExceeded. Then the user does something that restarts the feed in the same session: Up/Down map radius (app.mjs:407 applyPlace), alert radius or zone change (app.mjs:391 restartFeed), or the 'mapMoved' path.

Expected: within one launch, a failed save should still read back the latest value. Known items cover the quota pressure and silent map-save failures. This item is a separate logic bug: the memory fallback is hidden by a stale persisted copy.
confirmed.evidence: live.mjs:62 `get(k){try{const v=localStorage.getItem(k);if(v!==null)return JSON.parse(v);}catch{}return memory.get(k)??null;}` and :63 `set(k,v){memory.set(k,v);try{localStorage.setItem(k,JSON.stringify(v));}catch{}}`. Reproduced with a stubbed localStorage via node: set {seen:['a']} succeeds, quota then fills, set {seen:['a','b','c','d']} throws internally, and store.get returns {"seen":["a"]}.
confirmed.fix: Make memory authoritative for the session. In get, return memory.get(k) when memory.has(k), and only otherwise read localStorage (cache what it reads into memory). Or, in set's catch, remove the stale localStorage key so it cannot shadow the newer in-memory value. Ideally also report a failed set (return false) so callers such as the logbook can trim and retry.
