confirmed.title: Departures split-flap cells almost never flip in live use: the flip class comes from one shared parity counter, not from each cell
confirmed.trigger: Departures layout, live feed. Each render makes 49 setFlaps calls (1 clock + 8 rows x 6 columns). The live source renders twice per poll: once after the adsb.fi poll and once after route enrichment (live.mjs startLive: onUpdate in poll() and again in enrich()). Board values change only on the poll render, so a changed cell's next change comes 98 calls later. The clock's minute changes every 60 renders in demo (1 s ticks) and about every 24 renders live. Both counts are even.
confirmed.impact: setFlaps flips the module-global `flip` once per call and gives a changed cell class fb or fa from that global parity. When an even number of calls separates two changes to one cell, the cell gets the same class it already has. classList.remove/add then does nothing and the CSS animation (dep-flip-a/b) does not restart. In steady state the clock digits never flip, and neither do the Alt, Dist and Remarks cells that change once per poll. The text changes with no animation, so the layout's defining effect ('only the characters that change flip') is missing.
confirmed.evidence: departures.mjs:25 `flip^=1;` sits inside setFlaps, once per row group. Lines 30-31: `c.classList.remove(flip?'fa':'fb');c.classList.add(flip?'fb':'fa');`. render() at line 99 calls setFlaps($.clock) and then the 48 board calls (line 120). departures.css:21 runs the animation only through the .fa/.fb class change. live.mjs:300 calls onUpdate from enrich() and live.mjs:324 from poll(), so there are two renders per poll.
confirmed.fix: Alternate per cell, not globally, e.g. `const next=c.classList.contains('fa')?'fb':'fa';c.classList.remove('fa','fb');c.classList.add(next);`. Or restart the animation explicitly by removing the class, reading c.offsetWidth, then adding the class back.
reasons:
UPHELD: The claim holds up against the code. The line numbers in the claim are slightly off: `flip^=1` is at line 27 and the remove/add pair is at line 33.

1. **Parity alternates by render.** In web/layouts/departures.mjs, `setFlaps` toggles the module-global `flip` once per call. A changed cell gets class `fb` or `fa` from that global parity. Each `render()` makes 1 clock call (line 93) plus 8 rows × 6 columns = 48 board calls (lines 109-113), so 49 calls per render. Because 49 is odd, a given cell's parity flips each render. If two changes to one cell are an even number of renders apart, the cell gets the class it already has. `classList.remove(other)` then `add(same)` is a no-op, so the CSS animation (departures.css:21, `.c.fa`/`.c.fb`, keyframes dep-flip-a/b) does not restart. Changing `textContent` or `animationDelay` does not restart a finished animation either.

2. **Live mode renders twice per poll.** Rendering is driven by `onModel` (model.mjs:221, `liveSource`), which `app.mjs` `draw()` passes to `render`. `startLive` calls `onUpdate` in `poll()` (live.mjs:324) and then in `enrich()` (live.mjs:299). `enrich()` is not awaited and normally finishes within the poll interval, since route hits are cached or there is at most one adsb.lol request per 5 s. That makes 2 renders per poll.

3. **The second render changes nothing.** `airspace()` (core.mjs:89) takes positions, altitude and distance straight from the feed with no extrapolation by `now`. The enrich render therefore repeats the poll render's Alt, Dist and Remarks values and the row order. Board changes land on poll renders, which are always an even number of renders apart, so they never animate in steady state.

4. **The clock never flips either.** `fmt.clock` (kit.mjs:134) shows hours:minutes only. Live, the minute changes on a poll render, every 12 polls × 2 = 24 renders, which is even. In demo, `setInterval` fires every 1 s (model.mjs:291), so the minute changes every 60 renders, also even.

5. **When it does animate.** Only perturbations restore the effect: a failed poll (a single render), an `enrich` skipped because one is already running, or a route arriving on the enrich render. In demo, board cells change at irregular intervals, so they flip about half the time.

The defining "only changed characters flip" effect is effectively missing in live use. This is a real but cosmetic defect, so P3 is the right severity. The suggested fix (alternate per cell from its current class, or force a reflow between remove and add) is correct.

UPHELD: I could not refute this. In web/layouts/departures.mjs:25 `flip^=1` sits inside setFlaps, so it toggles once per call. In live mode the only render triggers are startLive's onUpdate, and app.mjs render→draw passes these straight through with no extra timer. onUpdate fires once in poll() (live.mjs:324) and once in enrich() (live.mjs:299), which poll calls right after rendering. Writing the same animationDelay value does not restart it either.

The clock behaves the same way. Live it gets about 12 polls x 2 = 24 renders per minute. Demo uses setInterval(tick,1000), which is 60 renders per minute. Both are even, so the clock's minute digits get the same class every time.

confirmed.title: Changing the map radius while map tiles can't be fetched wipes the map already on screen and leaves a blank map for minutes
confirmed.trigger: OpenFreeMap (tilejson or tiles) is unreachable or failing, for example during a network blip or provider outage. The user changes the map radius (Up/Down on the dashboard, or Settings > Map radius) to a radius that has no saved base map. Unsaved means it was never built, has dropped out of the 3 most recent radii (saveMap), or is more than 30 days old.
confirmed.impact: stepMap first redraws the current base map rescaled, so the map is still visible. 700 ms later applyPlace runs `if(!keepBase)maps.base=savedMap(place,range);`, which sets maps.base to null, and then calls mapsChanged(). paintMap clears the canvas and skips every base layer, so water, roads, runways, airport and airfield labels all disappear. Atlas shows 'Drawing the map…' and other layouts show an empty background, with 'Map unavailable'. buildMap then fails and retries after 30 s, 60 s, 90 s and so on, up to 5 min apart. The screen stays blank until a build succeeds or the user goes back to the old radius. The usable map that was in memory is thrown away, so a short outage turns into minutes of blank map. Expected: keep showing the previous map, rescaled as stepMap already does, until the new one is built.
confirmed.evidence: web/app.mjs:173-176: `const keepBase=same(maps.base)&&maps.base.range===range,...; if(!keepBase)maps.base=savedMap(place,range); ... if(!keepBase||!keepDetail)mapsChanged();`. savedMap (web/mapgen.mjs:331-336) returns null when no saved map exists for that exact range. The retry loop at web/app.mjs:182-195 only assigns maps.base after a successful buildMap and waits Math.min(300000,30000*(attempt+1)) between attempts. stepMap (web/app.mjs:398-408) does not clear maps.base, so the old map is drawn for the first 700 ms and then disappears. paintMap (web/kit.mjs:239-249) clears the canvas and skips layers whose map is null.

Replace it, and call mapsChanged, only when a saved map is found or buildMap succeeds. For example: `const saved=savedMap(place,range); if(saved||!same(maps.base))maps.base=saved;`. Every view already scales by zoom() and mapShift, so the old map draws correctly rescaled. Optionally show 'Map unavailable' over it rather than an empty canvas.

confirmed.title: If the silent loop fails to start once, it never retries for the rest of the session (and the failed player is leaked)
confirmed.trigger: Any rejection from VideoPlayer.initialize() or p.play() while 'Keep screen awake' is on. For example, at cold launch the media server is still coming up, or the media pipeline briefly refuses a session.
confirmed.impact: The .catch handler calls stopLoop(), which sets wanted=false. The only caller is the App.tsx useEffect keyed on [awake, active] (src/App.tsx:147), and neither value has changed, so startLoop() is never called again. Keep-awake stays off silently until the user backgrounds and reopens the app or toggles the setting off and on. The screensaver then appears even though Settings still shows Keep screen awake: On. Also, if the failure happens before `player = p` (in initialize(), or in the src or setSurfaceHandle setters), stopLoop() sees player==null and the half-initialized VideoPlayer `p` is never deinitialized. This is a different trigger from the known pause and chime cases: a start failure, not a later interruption.
confirmed.evidence: silentLoop.ts:30-49: `const p = new VideoPlayer(); await p.initialize(); ... player = p; await p.play(); })().catch(e => { console.error(...); stopLoop(); })`. stopLoop() (line 57) sets `wanted = false` and returns early when `player` is null. App.tsx:147-153 calls startLoop() only when `awake` or `active` changes. No retry timer or player error listener exists anywhere.
confirmed.fix: In the catch, deinitialize the local `p` if it was created and `player !== p`. Leave `wanted` unchanged instead of calling stopLoop(), and schedule a bounded retry, e.g. `setTimeout(() => { if (wanted && !player) startLoop(); }, 5000)` with back-off. Cancel that retry in stopLoop().
reasons: UPHELD: The code path is real. In src/silentLoop.ts:46-49, any rejection from initialize(), the setters, setSurfaceHandle or play() is caught and calls stopLoop(). stopLoop() (lines 57-63) sets wanted=false and returns early when player is null. If the failure happened before `player = p` (line 43), the local p is never deinitialized. If play() failed, player was already set to p, so stopLoop() does pause and deinitialize it. That means the leak only applies to failures before line 43. The only caller is the useEffect at src/App.tsx:147-153, keyed on [awake, active]. The page's 'awake' message (web/app.mjs:23) calls setAwake with the same boolean, and React skips re-running an effect when its dependencies are unchanged. So startLoop() runs again only when AppState changes state (background/inactive and back) or the user toggles the setting. There is no retry timer and no error listener. Settings keeps showing On while the loop is dead. Mitigating factors: the trigger (a media-pipeline start failure) is plausible but not shown to happen, and the 2 px surface and engage() reports continue. This is a robustness gap with low likelihood, so P3 stands.

UPHELD: I could not refute this claim. In src/silentLoop.ts:46-49, a rejection from initialize(), the src or setSurfaceHandle setters, or play() goes to the .catch handler. That handler calls stopLoop(), and stopLoop() sets wanted=false at line 58. Nothing else retries: there is no timer, no player error or ended listener, and the REASSERT_MS interval only calls engage() and never touches the loop. So after one start failure, the silent loop stays off until the user toggles the setting or the app goes to the background and comes back. Suggested fix: in the catch, deinitialize `p` when `player !== p`; leave `wanted` unchanged; schedule a bounded retry with back-off that runs only if `wanted && !player`; and clear that retry in stopLoop().

confirmed.title: Aircraft type from the feed is saved to 'Recently above' history with no length or type check, then redrawn and re-fitted on every poll after relaunch
confirmed.trigger: An adsb.fi entry inside the alert zone with a valid hex, position, alt_baro and seen_pos but a very long `t` (e.g. 300,000 characters) or a non-string `t`. selection() copies `aircraft_type:a.t??''` as is (live.mjs:89). mergeHistory() saves it (live.mjs:101), and store.set(HISTORY_KEY) runs on every poll that has the plane inside. On the read side, core.recentSightings() (core.mjs:121) trims only callsign and registration to 24 characters and passes aircraft_type through untouched. Live planes go through core.airspace(), which trims every field to 24 characters, so only the history path is open.
confirmed.impact: Checked with node: one such entry produces a 400,098-character history row (a 100k callsign plus a 300k type), and recentSightings returns aircraft_type with all 300,000 characters. The model then hands it to the layouts as a.aircraft_type or a.type. Cockpit (cockpit.mjs:206) and Radar (radar.mjs:192-197) put it in a span and call fitLine on it. fitLine shrinks the font in 0.5 px steps and forces a reflow of the whole string on each step, roughly 10-20 reflows per render on every poll (5-15 s) on the stick. In Atlas, the default layout, a long wrapping value makes the side column overflow, so 'Recently above' is hidden on every render. A non-string `t` shows as '[object Object]'. mergeHistory never ages rows out; they only leave when 20 newer sightings push them out. So the row survives relaunches and keeps costing reflows, plus about 0.8 MB of localStorage, which is already near quota. In a quiet area that can last days. Expected: the type is limited to a short ICAO designator, as it is for live planes.
confirmed.evidence: live.mjs:89 `aircraft_type:a.t??''`; live.mjs:101 the history row keeps `aircraft_type:a.aircraft_type`; core.mjs:120-121 recentSightings spreads `...a` and trims only `callsign` and `registration`; model.mjs liveSource maps recent rows to `type:typeName(a.aircraft_type)` (typeName returns the code itself when unknown); cockpit.mjs:206 `el('span','',...a.aircraft_type||'')` then fitLine(s) at :208; kit.mjs:180 is the fitLine reflow loop. node check: JSON.stringify(history).length = 400098, recent[0].callsign.length = 24, recent[0].aircraft_type.length = 300000.
confirmed.fix: Clean the feed fields when they enter history. In selection(), set aircraft_type to typeof a.t==='string' ? a.t.trim().slice(0,24) : '', and limit callsign and registration the same way. Also clean aircraft_type in recentSightings, and validate aircraft_type in mergeHistory's carry-over loop, so rows already saved by older builds are fixed on read. A stricter /^[A-Z0-9]{2,4}$/ designator check also stops keys like 'constructor' or '__proto__' from reaching log.typesAll.

The path is real and it reproduces. poll() (live.mjs:319-320) calls selection() and then mergeHistory(), and store.set(HISTORY_KEY) runs on every poll that has a plane inside. selection() copies `aircraft_type:a.t??''` unchecked (live.mjs:89), and mergeHistory() keeps it (live.mjs:101). I ran it in node: a 300,000-character `t` came out of recentSightings at 300,000 characters, and an object `t` came out as an object. The only built-in limit is the bridge's 2 MB response cap (App.tsx:34), which allows this size. The fix is to cap `t`, callsign and registration in selection(), and to clean aircraft_type again in recentSightings. Why it stays P3: the trigger needs adsb.fi, a trusted feed reached over TLS, to send a malformed or oversized `t`, which its database does not produce in normal operation. So this is hardening against a bad upstream, not a user-reachable bug. I did not verify the claimed render costs (fitLine reflow counts, the Atlas overflow, localStorage near quota) on a device.

confirmed.title: At the 150 and 250 mi map radii, one failed adsb.fi poll clears every aircraft and shows 'No signal' for a full 15 s cycle
confirmed.trigger: Set Map radius to 150 or 250 mi. That makes pollSeconds 15 (web/app.mjs:38). Then let one feed poll fail: a 4 s timeout on the large wide-area payload, a 429, an HTML error page that parses as 'invalid', or a brief Wi-Fi drop.
confirmed.impact: Observed: on the failed poll, live.mjs:326 calls onUpdate(states,false) with the previous payload. liveSource then computes now-lastOk (about 15 s plus the failure latency), so the 15000 ms 'connected' check (model.mjs:208) fails. Even if it passed, airspace() (core.mjs:93) rejects the feed because its stamp is now more than 15 s old. Either way all=[] and every plane, the hero and the alert-zone count disappear. Layouts switch to 'No signal' and 'No live data right now'. The next attempt only comes a full interval later (live.mjs:327), so the screen stays blank for at least 15 s per missed poll. Two things make it worse. First, the feed request keeps a fixed 4000 ms timeout (live.mjs:315) even though the same endpoint at 250 NM gets 8000 ms in checkCoverage (live.mjs:309), so the widest and slowest payloads are the ones most likely to time out. Second, at 10 s cadence (25-100 mi) a timed-out poll leaves the data about 14 s old, so the per-plane check age+seen_pos<=20 (core.mjs:98) quietly drops aircraft whose seen_pos is above about 6 s. Expected: one missed poll is tolerated, as it is at the default 5 s cadence (about 2 misses before going stale), and the last positions stay on screen.
confirmed.evidence: I ran airspace() from web/core.mjs with a two-aircraft feed and seen_pos of 1 and 4. At stamp+0.3 s (connected) it returned 2 planes, fresh=true. confirmed.title: Choosing a place at the same coordinates saves it but keeps the old time zone and elevation, so the dashboard clock stays wrong until relaunch
confirmed.trigger: A place is saved with the wrong time zone, for example a Census or Nominatim address whose time-zone lookup failed and fell back to America/New_York or UTC (known place.mjs:102). The user sees the wrong clock and fixes it the obvious way: Settings > Location, search the same address again (same geocoder, so identical coordinates, and the time-zone lookup now succeeds), then 'Use this'. confirmed.title: Route lookups need a stick clock at or ahead of adsb.fi's, while the plane display allows 5 s behind: if the clock lags slightly, no routes ever appear
confirmed.trigger: The Fire TV clock runs behind adsb.fi's `now` stamp by more than the network latency plus the server cache age (roughly 0.5 to 1 s; for example before NTP sync or with a drifting clock). Then Date.now()/1000 - stamp is less than 0 on every poll.

No ADSB.lol lookups run, no sightings are recorded, 'Recently above' route recovery is disabled, and every hero card and Departures row shows a blank route for as long as the clock lags, with no error shown. History rows whose last_seen is slightly in the future are also dropped (line 123: now - a.last_seen >= 0). Expected: routes follow the same freshness window as the display. This is different from the known skew finding at live.mjs:85: here the two freshness windows disagree, so routes alone go dark.
confirmed.evidence: live.mjs:81 `fresh=age>=-5&&age<=15` versus live.mjs:120 `if(!(now-stamp>=0&&now-stamp<=15)...) return [];`. Checked with node: stamp=1000000, now=stamp-1, one aircraft with seen_pos=2. selection().inside.length=1 and airspace().all.length=1, but observations().length=0.

The failure is silent, because enrich() has no error path. confirmed.title: At wide map radii the single ADSB.lol lookup per poll goes to whichever aircraft has the freshest position, including ones never drawn, so the hero's route can stay blank for many minutes

The 'Approaching' or 'Nearest' hero, or the nearest planes on the map, get no priority over aircraft 200 NM away that are off the map. With N uncached callsigns, a given plane waits about N/2 polls (for example 150 x 10 s, about 25 min), while hits expire after 1 h. The hero card and nearby labels often show no route for the plane the viewer is looking at.

confirmed.title: A place with no time-zone field passes validation as timeZone undefined: the clock shows '—' forever and the logbook day and 'Cargo tonight' use the TV's time zone

Missing, null or invalid values otherwise become 'UTC'. model.start sets TZ=undefined. core.localClock skips because timeZone is falsy and shows '—' permanently. model.localDay/localHour silently fall back to the device zone, which the code comment says it must never do. The logbook midnight reset, DST handling and the 18:00-06:00 'Cargo tonight' window then follow the TV's zone rather than home's. The place is re-saved the same way on every launch, so it never recovers.
confirmed.evidence: Checked with node: validTz(undefined)=true, validTz('')=false, validTz(null)=false. place.mjs:43 `const timeZone=validTz(o.timeZone)?o.timeZone:'UTC'`. core.mjs:12 `if (timeZone) try {...}` returns '—' otherwise. model.mjs:78-79 pass `timeZone:TZ` (undefined) to toLocale*.

confirmed.title: Negative barometric altitudes print as '0-1', '0-3' in the Radar, Sectional and Synthwave aircraft tags
confirmed.trigger: Altitude in feet. An aircraft reports a negative alt_baro, which is normal for pressure altitude near sea level on a high-pressure day (e.g. on short final at a coastal airport at 1030 hPa, alt_baro of about -100 to -400 ft). The feed accepts any numeric alt_baro (live.mjs:85).
confirmed.impact: blockText computes String(Math.round(ft/100)).padStart(3,'0'): for -100 ft that gives '-1'.padStart(3,'0') = '0-1', and for -300 ft it gives '0-3'. The aircraft's data block shows garbage altitude text. The same expression appears in sectional.mjs:189 (tag line 2) and synthwave.mjs:127 (tag line 2). A value between -50 and 0 rounds to -0 and shows '000'. Expected: a signed flight-level figure such as '-01' (as Cockpit's relAlt does), or the ground/low-altitude wording.
confirmed.evidence: radar.mjs:110 `String(Math.round(ft/100)).padStart(3,'0')`; sectional.mjs:189 `String(Math.round((a.altitude_ft||0)/100)).padStart(3,'0')`; synthwave.mjs:127 `String(Math.round((a.altitude_ft||0)/100)).padStart(3,'0')`. In JS, '-1'.padStart(3,'0') === '0-1'.
confirmed.fix: Add one kit helper, e.g. fmt.fl100(ft): v=Math.round(ft/100); return (v<0?'-':'')+String(Math.abs(v)).padStart(v<0?2:3,'0'). Use it in all three layouts, or clamp to 0 and show 'GND/000' for values below 0.

They copy it to altitude_ft without clamping, so a negative value gets through; the string 'ground' is still rejected. model.mjs and the three layouts filter aircraft by ground distance only, with no altitude floor. So a negative-altitude aircraft near home is drawn and can be tagged. Altitude is in feet by default (kit.mjs:125: altUnit is 'ft' unless S.altitude is 'm'), and in feet the tags use the cited expression: radar.mjs:110, sectional.mjs:189 and synthwave.mjs:127. Running it in node confirms the output: String(Math.round(-100/100)).padStart(3,'0') gives '0-1', and -30 ft gives '000'. Cockpit's relAlt (cockpit.mjs:107-110) already handles the sign, which shows the intended format. ADS-B feeds do report negative pressure altitudes for aircraft landing or taking off at low-elevation airports on high-pressure days. The effect is only garbled tag text, with no crash or data loss, so P3 is right.

confirmed.title: Atlas labels airports and place names only in the inner ~70% of the map. The label windows were not updated when commit e462e19 rescaled the map (54 to 25.5 px/mi).
confirmed.trigger: Any Atlas or Atlas Dark view at any map radius R. Example: R = 10 mi with a coded airport or town 8-10 mi north or south of <home>, or a town 8-13 mi east or west.
confirmed.impact: Commit e462e19 made the whole radius visible. Atlas now draws about 1.05R north, 0.9R south and 1.37R east/west of home. airfieldsNear(maps,7) still only keeps airfields with |y| < 0.7R and |x| < 1.05R. placesNear(maps,7) only keeps places with |x|,|y| < 0.7R. So the outer band of the map has roads, water and runways, and aircraft are drawn over it, but airports and towns there get no ring marker or name. At 25 and 50 mi a second limit applies: small coded fields exist only in the z10 airfield pass (mapgen.mjs:180), which is still sized for the old 0.7x-sideways view (flim = 0.85R). Fields between 0.85R and the 1.05R label limit east or west are therefore missing from the data entirely. Expected: labels cover the area the map now shows.
confirmed.evidence: Before e462e19: VIEW ppm 54 showed 276/54 = 5.1 mi north and 350/54 = 6.5 mi sideways, so within=7 covered the whole view. Now VIEW = {cx:350, cy:276, ppm:25.5} (atlas.mjs:13), but drawMap still calls airfieldsNear(maps,7) and placesNear(maps,7,{max:60}) (atlas.mjs:196-197). kit.mjs:302-306: placesNear uses range = within/zoom() = 0.7R and keeps |x|<range && |y|<range. kit.mjs:316-319: airfieldsNear keeps |x| < range*1.5 && |y| < range. mapgen.mjs:180-181 still says 'Atlas ... sees ~0.7x the radius sideways' and sets flim = range*.85. One option is to pass separate x/y extents, or to filter by toView() falling inside the existing label bounds instead of a miles box. In mapgen.mjs, raise the z10 airfield pass to flim ≈ 1.4R (and update the stale comment) so coded fields across the whole Atlas view are collected at 25 and 50 mi. Extend scripts/check-drawn.mjs to assert that every coded airfield inside the canvas gets a marker.

At R = 10 the map canvas therefore shows about 13.7 mi to each side (350/25.5), 10.8 mi north (276/25.5) and 10.35 mi south (264/25.5).

UPHELD: The claim holds up. kit.mjs:70 defines zoom() as BASE_RANGE/range() with BASE_RANGE=10, so placesNear(maps,7) at kit.mjs:301-306 keeps places with |x| and |y| under 0.7R. airfieldsNear(maps,7) at kit.mjs:314-317 keeps airfields with |x| < 1.05R and |y| < 0.7R. confirmed.title: A 29-byte vector tile makes the bundled MVT decoder allocate without limit (ClosePath repeat count), so the WebView runs out of memory on every map build
confirmed.trigger: Any tile from tiles.openfreemap.org (or whatever host the TileJSON names that TILE_URL accepts) holds a feature in a layer mapgen reads ('water', 'place', 'aerodrome_label', 'transportation', and others) whose geometry is MoveTo(0,0), then a ClosePath command with a huge repeat count (e.g. 268,000,000), then one trailing byte. mapgen.mjs:97-107 calls f.loadGeometry() on it. In loadGeometry, `while(t.pos<e){if(o<=0){read cmd}; o--; ... else if(n===7) r&&r.push(r[0].clone())}`: ClosePath reads no bytes, so the trailing byte keeps t.pos<e true and the loop runs the full count, pushing one new Point per pass. The MVT spec allows only a count of 1 for ClosePath, and nothing here checks it.
confirmed.impact: Reproduced in node with web/mvt.js as shipped. A 28-byte tile with count 4,000,000 gives 4,000,002 points and 224 MB of heap in 157 ms. A 29-byte tile with count 268,000,000 ends in 'FATAL ERROR: ... JavaScript heap out of memory'. On the stick the WebView renderer would die, which leaves the known black screen with keep-awake still asserted. The 2 MB bridge cap and the reported 'no size cap before decode' issue do not cover this, because the payload is tiny. A failed build is never saved, so every launch fetches the same tile again and crashes again, until the tile server stops serving it. The only precondition is a misbehaving or compromised third-party tile server; nothing on the device has to change.
confirmed.evidence: Scratch script /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-the owner-Documents-ChatGPT-Vibe-Coding/2afc01d9-34cf-4185-ae38-d85a302dd1ae/scratchpad/mvt-bomb.cjs loads web/mvt.js and builds the tile bytes [layer 'water', feature type 3, geometry 9,0,0,<varint count*8+7>,15]. Its output was 'points 4000002 ms 157 heapMB 224', and with count=268000000 under --max-old-space-size=1024 the process aborted on heap exhaustion. The decoder loop is in web/mvt.js loadGeometry (minified, line 1), and it is called with no limit at web/mapgen.mjs:99, :100 and :107.
confirmed.fix: Bound the geometry decode. In loadGeometry (and in bbox), reject ClosePath with a count other than 1, or stop when the number of points produced goes above the geometry byte length (each real point needs at least 2 bytes), e.g. `if(n===7&&o>0) throw new Error('bad ClosePath')`. Also put each feature's decode in eachTile inside a try/catch, so one bad feature drops only that feature and not the whole map, and add an overall per-tile point budget (for example 200k points).
reasons:
UPHELD: The bug is real, but I'd rate it P3, not P2, because it only happens if the tile server is malicious or compromised.

**Evidence:**
- I rebuilt the tile independently with web/mvt.js as shipped: layer 'water', feature type 3, geometry [9,0,0,varint(N*8+7),15]. The whole tile is 28 bytes.
- With N=1,000,000, loadGeometry() returned a ring of 1,000,002 points in 26 ms. The ClosePath command reads no bytes, so the trailing byte keeps the loop running for the full repeat count, and nothing in the decoder checks it.
- The call path is real. app.mjs:185 and app.mjs:563 call buildMap. buildMap calls eachTile, which decodes each fetched tile with new MVT.VectorTile. The geom, point and shore helpers then call f.loadGeometry() with no limit and no try/catch around each feature.
- TILE_URL (mapgen.mjs:14) only checks that the URL is tiles.openfreemap.org/planet/..., not what the tile contains. So a tile from that host reaches the decoder unchanged.

**Why it is lower than P2:**
- It needs the third-party tile server (OpenFreeMap) to be malicious or compromised; a normal outage or a corrupt file will not produce this byte pattern.
- A legitimate encoder never writes this pattern, and it would not happen by accident.
- What it causes is denial of service (the map build crashes the WebView), not code execution or a data leak.

The suggested fix is still sound: reject a ClosePath count other than 1, and add a per-tile point budget and a per-feature try/catch.

UPHELD: I could not refute the mechanism. The ClosePath branch in loadGeometry in web/mvt.js (minified, line 1) reads no bytes, and the loop condition is only t.pos<e. So a single command header with count up to about 2^28, followed by one trailing byte, pushes one point per pass, and nothing checks for a count other than 1. The callers in web/mapgen.mjs (geom at :99, point at :100, shore at :107) call f.loadGeometry() with no point budget. The try/catch blocks at :188, :320 and :334 would not help, because running out of memory is not an exception JS can catch, and the 2 MB MAX_BYTES cap in src/App.tsx:34 does not apply to a 29-byte payload. A failed buildMap is never saved (web/app.mjs:185-187), so the app would try again on the next launch. I am lowering the severity from P2 to P3 for two reasons. First, the tile host is pinned to HTTPS tiles.openfreemap.org in both the page (mapgen.mjs:14 TILE_URL) and the native allow-list (App.tsx:27/31). The trigger therefore needs that specific third-party server to be compromised or to have a broken tile generator; real tile generators only ever write a ClosePath count of 1. Second, the same unbounded behavior is in upstream @mapbox/vector-tile, so this is a hardening gap that an unlikely event would expose, not a failure that ordinary use would hit. The suggested fix is cheap and correct: reject ClosePath with a count other than 1, or cap points at the geometry byte length divided by 2.

UPHELD: The mechanism is real, but P2 overstates it. In web/mvt.js, loadGeometry runs `for(;t.pos<e;){if(o<=0){...o=d>>3...} o--, ...}`, and ClosePath (n===7) reads no bytes, so a huge ClosePath count with a trailing byte makes the loop push one point per pass. Nothing checks for this. mapgen.mjs:99, :100 and :107 call loadGeometry with no limit. The main eachTile pass in buildMap (mapgen.mjs:134) is not wrapped in a try/catch, though a try/catch would not stop an out-of-memory crash anyway. buildMap is called from app.mjs:185 and :563.

The trigger is the weak part. TILE_URL (mapgen.mjs:14) pins tiles to https://tiles.openfreemap.org/planet/..., so the attack needs a malicious or compromised OpenFreeMap, or an HTTPS man-in-the-middle. No honest encoder emits ClosePath with a count other than 1, so ordinary users will never hit this. It is a robustness gap against an adversarial upstream, not a bug that occurs in normal use. If the tile provider were compromised, it could already degrade the map badly with legitimate dense geometry under the 2 MB cap. The tiny-payload amplification is the only new part.

The 'crash on every launch' persistence argument holds only while the hostile server keeps serving the tile. Bounding the decode is still worth doing: reject ClosePath when the count is not 1, and cap points per byte or per tile. This is hardening (P3), not a P2 user-facing defect.

confirmed.title: A map past 30 days old is discarded before a new one is fetched, so an offline launch (or a tile outage) shows a blank map even though a usable map is saved
confirmed.trigger: Saved place, base and street maps built 30 or more days ago (a stick in daily use reaches this once a month). The app launches while the network is down, DNS fails, OpenFreeMap is down or returns 429, or the stick's clock jumps forward before NTP sync. Any later radius change or applyPlace in the same state does the same.
confirmed.impact: savedMap() returns null when Date.now()-m.built>=MAX_AGE, so applyPlace (web/app.mjs:176) sets maps.base=null and calls mapsChanged(). The layout repaints with no water, roads, airports or place labels. The only path to a map is buildMap, which throws at tileTemplate while offline. The loop then shows 'Map unavailable, retrying…' and backs off to 5-minute retries until the network returns. In detail layouts (the default Atlas Dark among them), savedDetail (web/mapgen.mjs:359) applies the same cut-off. ensureDetail then fails once with 'Street map unavailable' and, as already reported, is never retried, so the street map stays gone for the session. The old map data is still in localStorage and would have drawn correctly. Expected: show the old map and refresh it in the background, replacing it only after a successful rebuild.
confirmed.evidence: web/mapgen.mjs:213-217 savedMap: `same=...&&Date.now()-m.built<MAX_AGE; return same?m:null;`. web/mapgen.mjs:355-360 savedDetail has the same `Date.now()-m.built<MAX_AGE?m:null`. web/app.mjs:176 `if(!keepBase)maps.base=savedMap(place,range);` then mapsChanged() at :178. The retry loop at web/app.mjs:186-198 only assigns maps.base after buildMap succeeds. web/app.mjs:135-150 ensureDetail: `saved=savedDetail(place,spec)` null leads to buildDetail; on failure it sets 'Street map unavailable' with no retry.
confirmed.fix: Split 'usable' from 'fresh'. Have savedMap/savedDetail return a map that matches the place, version and spec whatever its age, with a stale flag. In applyPlace/ensureDetail, draw the stale map at once and start the rebuild in the background (the existing retry loop), swapping it in only after saveMap/saveDetail succeeds. Also treat a negative or far-future `built` age (clock not yet synced) as fresh instead of expired.
reasons:
UPHELD: The code path is real. MAX_AGE is 30 days (web/mapgen.mjs:15). savedMap (mapgen.mjs:213-217) and savedDetail (mapgen.mjs:355-360) return null once Date.now()-m.built>=MAX_AGE, and they also return null when a clock jump makes that difference huge. applyPlace (app.mjs:176) then sets maps.base=null and calls mapsChanged() before any rebuild is tried. The retry loop (app.mjs:186-198) only fills maps.base after buildMap succeeds. ensureDetail (app.mjs:135-150) moves on to buildDetail and shows 'Street map unavailable'. The old entry stays in localStorage and would match the place, version and range, but nothing reads it. So an offline or tile-outage launch past 30 days shows a blank map until the network returns.

The impact is narrower than claimed:
(1) A map already in memory survives because keepBase keeps it, so a session that runs continuously is unaffected. It only bites on a launch, a radius change or an applyPlace that happens while offline, after the map has expired.
(2) In the most common case, a full network outage, the adsb.fi feed is also down, so the screen has no aircraft anyway and the blank map adds little harm. The case that really hurts is OpenFreeMap failing or rate-limiting while the feed works, or the clock jumping forward before NTP sync.
(3) Nothing is lost for good. saveMap only overwrites after a successful build, and the retry loop recovers once tiles are reachable.
(4) The claim that the detail map is 'never retried' is overstated. ensureDetail runs again on a layout switch (app.mjs:119) and on a later applyPlace.

This is a real but limited robustness defect. The fix to show the stale map while rebuilding in the background is sound. P3, not P2.

In web/mapgen.mjs, lines 213-217 (savedMap) and 355-360 (savedDetail) return null once Date.now()-m.built>=MAX_AGE (30 days, line 15). confirmed.title: Base-map cache evicts by build order, not use: the map in daily use (for example the default 10 mi) is deleted before a wider map that was tried once
confirmed.trigger: 1. Build maps at 10, 25 and 50 mi (recent list becomes [50,25,10]). 2. Go back to 10 mi and 25 mi. Both load from cache through savedMap, and the recent list is not touched. 3. Observed: the radius in daily use is deleted. Returning to it rebuilds the whole tile set, with a 'Map unavailable' / blank map if the tiles can't be fetched at that moment (offline or tile outage), even though the user never stopped using that radius. Reproduced with stubbed localStorage: after save 10, 25, 50 -> load 10, 25 from cache -> save 100, savedMap(home,10) returns null while savedMap(home,50) is still present.
confirmed.evidence: saveMap (web/mapgen.mjs:219-224) is the only place RECENT_KEY ('whatsup.map.recent') is reordered, and it runs only after buildMap. savedMap (web/mapgen.mjs:213-218) returns a cached map without updating RECENT_KEY. app.mjs applyPlace (around line 176-182) takes the cached path `maps.base=savedMap(place,range); ... if(maps.base){startFeed();return;}` and never calls saveMap, so a cache hit doesn't count as use. node -e test: `10 cached? true 25 cached? true` then `after 100: 10 cached? false 50 cached? true`.
confirmed.fix: When savedMap returns a hit, move its range to the front of RECENT_KEY without rewriting the map, so eviction is truly least-recently-used: `const touch=r=>store.set(RECENT_KEY,[r,...(store.get(RECENT_KEY)||[]).filter(x=>x!==r)].slice(0,3));`, called from savedMap on success (or from applyPlace's cache-hit path). Optionally never evict the default CONFIG.rangeMiles slot.

It evicts every range after the first three, in list order. savedMap (213-218) reads the cache and never touches the recent list. In web/app.mjs:176, applyPlace sets maps.base=savedMap(place,range), and at line 182 it returns on a cache hit (`if(maps.base){startFeed();return;}`). saveMap runs only after buildMap succeeds (line 187), so loading a map from cache never counts as use. The claimed order is right: save 10, 25, 50 gives [50,25,10]. Loading 10 and 25 from cache leaves that unchanged. Saving 100 gives [100,50,25,10], which removes keyFor(10), the original 'whatsup.map.v2' key, while the 50 mi map tried once stays. All maps expire after MAX_AGE (30 days) anyway. It takes four distinct radii to trigger. The cost is one extra tile rebuild, and the map is blank only if tiles can't be fetched at that moment. P3 is the right severity. The suggested fix is sound: move the range to the front of the recent list on a savedMap hit.

rejected.title: Place label prints a JavaScript function's source when the geocoder's region is an Object.prototype name; the label is saved to Settings
reasons: REFUTED: The function behaves as claimed. In web/place.mjs:34, `US[admin]` reads inherited properties, and running placeLabel({name:'Springfield',admin:'constructor',countryCode:'US'}) does print the Object constructor's source. The trigger cannot happen in practice, though. The admin value never comes from the user. It is always a region field returned by a geocoder for a real place: Open-Meteo admin1, Nominatim address.state, Census addressComponents.state, or GeoJS region. A country code of US or CA also has to be present. Those services return real state and province names or codes for US and CA places, and none of them is named 'constructor', 'toString', 'valueOf' or 'hasOwnProperty'. The user can search for the text 'constructor', but that only changes the place name. The region still comes from the service's own data. In the Census path, `STATE_NAME[a.state]||a.state` would yield a function only for the same impossible state code, and clean() then turns that into ''. To hit the bug, a third-party service would have to return a fake region name, and an attacker able to do that could send far more harmful data anyway. The outcome would also be a confusing label, not a crash or a security hole. Using Object.hasOwn would be a fine hardening change, but this is not a defect that real input can reach.

REFUTED: The code path is real but cannot be reached in practice, so it is not a defect worth shipping a fix for. At web/place.mjs:34, placeLabel looks up US[admin] and CA[admin] on plain object literals (lines 17-25). A string such as 'constructor' would pick up the inherited Object function, and nothing guards against that. However, admin only ever comes from Open-Meteo admin1, Census/Nominatim state names, or GeoJS region. Those are real first-level administrative names (US states, Canadian provinces), and none of these services returns 'constructor', 'toString', 'valueOf' or 'hasOwnProperty' as a state for a US or CA result. The only way to get there is a geocoder sending fabricated data. A provider doing that could already put any misleading text into name or admin, which clean() passes through by design, so this adds no new exposure. The worst result is wrong text in a city label, which the user can fix by picking another place. No crash, no data loss and no security effect. searchAddress (place.mjs:118) is harmless, as the claim itself says. The hasOwn change is a cheap hardening, but there is no realistic trigger, so this does not qualify as a concrete defect.

REFUTED: The code behavior is real. web/place.mjs:34 looks up US[admin] and CA[admin] on plain object literals (lines 17-27), so an admin of 'constructor' or 'valueOf' would return the inherited function, and placeLabel would put its source in the label. The trigger cannot happen in practice, though. admin is only ever filled from Open-Meteo admin1 (searchPlaces), GeoJS region (locateByIp), Census state (searchAddress, after a STATE_NAME lookup) or Nominatim address.state. The bug only applies when countryCode is US or CA. For those countries, all four services return real first-level divisions, such as 'Ohio', 'Ontario' or a two-letter state code. None of them is named 'constructor', 'toString', 'valueOf', 'hasOwnProperty' or any other Object.prototype key. The replies come over HTTPS through the native allow-listed fetch bridge, so the user cannot type the value in, and no other path writes it. The only way to get such a value is a geocoder bug or a compromised provider, and that attacker could show any text anyway. The worst case is an odd label that the user can fix by picking another place, with no crash or data loss. This is a hardening nit (Object.hasOwn or Object.create(null) would be a fine one-line change), not a defect a TV user will ever see.

rejected.title: The adsb.fi poll has a fixed 4 s timeout at every map radius, so on a modest connection the 100–250 mi feeds never finish and the app shows 'No signal'
reasons: REFUTED: The code path exists, but the failure it claims is not shown. web/live.mjs:315 does pass a fixed 4000 ms to getJson for every searchNm, and src/App.tsx:69-93 does abort the fetch at that point even while response.text() is still reading. A timeout returns 'connection_error', poll() then calls onUpdate(states,false), and model.mjs:204-221 shows 'No signal' after 15 s with no successful poll. The claim that wide-radius polls never finish rests on two guesses, and neither is backed by evidence. (1) It counts bytes as uncompressed JSON. When I gzip the repo's own fixture, tests/fixtures/chicago-feed.json (55 aircraft, 30,861 B), it shrinks to 5,645 B, about 5.5x smaller. If adsb.fi gzips its JSON, as most JSON APIs do, a 1.5 MB reply is about 275 KB on the wire. That takes about 2.2 s at 1 Mbps and under 1 s at 3 Mbps, inside the 4 s budget. Whether this server compresses was not checked, but nothing shows that it does not. (2) The '1–3 Mbps useful throughput' TV link is assumed, not observed, and nothing shows adsb.fi takes long to build the reply. So 'every poll fails, permanently No signal' is not established. What remains is a reasonable hardening idea: scale the timeout with radius, as the 8000 ms coverage probe at live.mjs:309 already does for the same 250 NM area. That only matters on very slow links or a slow server, and on those a single timed-out poll is retried every 10–15 s. Treat it as a low-priority robustness improvement, not a confirmed P2.

REFUTED: The code matches the claim, but its impact rests on an assumption that does not hold. web/live.mjs:315 does pass a fixed 4000 ms timeout, App.tsx get() (src/App.tsx:64-94, clamp at 211-214) aborts during response.text(), and a failed poll calls onUpdate(states,false). If that kept happening, lastOk would stay unset and 'No signal' would show after 15 s (web/model.mjs:204-221).

The failure only follows if a 0.5-1.5 MB body has to cross a 1-3 Mbps link. That is the uncompressed JSON size taken from the fixture. The browser's fetch and Vega's native fetch both send Accept-Encoding: gzip and decompress transparently. Aircraft JSON is highly repetitive and compresses to roughly 10-20%, so the real transfer is about 100-250 KB, which takes well under 2 s even at 1-3 Mbps. So 'never finish on a modest connection' is not shown. It would only happen on links much slower than the trigger states, or when adsb.fi itself responds slowly.

The 'every poll fails' and '5,760 wasted responses a day' figures assume a failure the evidence does not show. The 8000 ms coverage-probe timeout is a deliberate allowance for a rare 30-minute call and does not prove that 4 s is too short. Nothing in the repo shows a timeout at wide radii. A timeout that scales with the area would still be a reasonable hardening step, but this is not a concrete P2 defect.

REFUTED: The code details are correct. poll() at web/live.mjs:315 always uses 4000 ms. The coverage probe at :309 uses 8000 ms. App.tsx get() aborts, even while response.text() is still reading the body, and returns 'connection_error'. That would leave lastOk unset and show 'No signal' (web/model.mjs:206-221, kit.mjs:149).

The claimed impact does not hold up, though. The byte maths assumes uncompressed JSON on the wire. adsb.fi-style JSON compresses heavily: gzipping tests/fixtures/chicago-feed.json takes it from 30,861 to 5,645 bytes, about 5.5x smaller. So a 0.5-1.5 MB reply is roughly 90-270 KB on the wire, which takes about 0.3-2.2 s at 1-3 Mbps and fits inside 4 s. Nothing in src/ or native/ disables content encoding, and standard RN/OkHttp/curl-style fetch stacks send Accept-Encoding: gzip by default. Not verified for Vega, but nothing points the other way.

The trigger also needs two things together: a TV getting only about 1-3 Mbps of useful throughput on home Wi-Fi (unusual for a streaming device), and the user choosing the widest non-default radius. Even then a failure is not permanent. Any single poll that finishes inside 4 s sets lastOk, so the status flaps rather than staying 'No signal' forever. The '5,760 wasted large responses a day' figure assumes every poll fails, which is not realistic.

What is left is a minor inconsistency: the wide-area poll timeout could scale with searchNm, as the coverage probe already does. This is worth a cheap hardening tweak, but it is not a P2 user-facing defect.

critic:
I found 10 new defects not on the known lists, all from reading the code: 1 P1, 2 P2 and 7 P3. Nothing in the repo was changed and no network calls were made. For the areas that had no new code defect, I say what I checked. Areas that can only be checked on a device or outside the code are listed at the end.

**New defects**

1. **[P1] Accessibility: VoiceView gets nothing to read** (web/app.mjs:223, web/index.html:21)
   - Trigger: VoiceView turned on, user moves through Settings, the keyboard or the confirm screens.
   - Observed: `setFocus` only toggles a `.focus` CSS class. Nothing in web/ calls `.focus()`, and there is not a single `aria-label`. The only live region is the toast. Keydown arrows are swallowed with `preventDefault`, so focus changes, screen changes and hero changes are never announced.
     - The picker arrows are bare "‹" / "›" glyphs.
     - The overlays have no dialog role, and the dashboard behind them is not hidden from the screen reader.
   - Expected: each focus move announces the row or key, with its value.
   - Fix: give every `[data-focus]` element `tabindex=-1` and call `el.focus({preventScroll:true})` in `setFocus`. Add `aria-label` to the picker arrows and `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal` to the overlays. Set `aria-hidden` on `#layout` while a layer is open. Add a polite live region for the hero status line. Then check on a device that VoiceView still passes D-pad keys through to the page.

2. **[P3] Accessibility: low contrast and small text** (web/whatsup.css:35, web/layouts/glass.css:12 and :59, web/app.mjs:16)
   - Trigger: any theme.
   - Observed:
     - The Adjust position privacy note (`.note.small`, index.html:113) is 11 px in `--ui-faint`. Its contrast is 1.83:1 on Atlas Light, 2.27 on Atlas Dark, 2.58 on Blueprint, 2.59 on the default green and about 2.07 on Glass. The WCAG minimum is 4.5:1.
     - Glass place names are 2.29:1.
     - About 40 text styles are under 12 px on the 960×540 stage, which is 24 px at 1080p. Glass `.gl-mini span` is 8.5 px, so 17 px at 1080p.
     - The stage scales only with the viewport (app.mjs:16), so the system text-size setting has no effect.
   - Expected: at least 4.5:1 for informative text, and a readable minimum size.
   - Fix: use `--ui-dim` for `.note.small`, raise the alpha of `.gl-place`, and set a floor of about 12 px on the stage.

3. **[P2] 24 h+ soak: the whole logbook is rewritten to localStorage twice per poll** (web/model.mjs:218, web/live.mjs:299)
   - Trigger: any session with a fresh feed. Both the poll's `onUpdate` and the enrichment's `onUpdate` run `updateLog` followed by `store.set(LOG_KEY)`.
   - Observed: `log.planes` takes every drawn aircraft at any distance, up to 4000 per day. I measured the JSON at **358 KB at the cap** with a node simulation. In a busy area that means about 2 × 358 KB of synchronous stringify plus write every 5 to 15 s, which is gigabytes of flash writes per day and main-thread stalls on a 1 GB stick.
   - Expected: write only when the log actually changed, and at most every 30 to 60 s.
   - Fix: add a dirty flag and a throttled save, skip the second save from the enrichment path, and keep the per-plane map small (for example only planes within the map radius).

4. **[P3] Non-US locales: date is in British order for US users** (web/kit.mjs:135)
   - Trigger: any US place, on Atlas, Glass, Night Sky, Synthwave, Radar, Blueprint and Sectional.
   - Observed: `fmt.date` is hard-coded to `en-GB`, so US users see "Wednesday 28 October" and "Wed 28 Oct" (checked with node).
   - Expected: "Wednesday, October 28" in the US.
   - Fix: pick the locale the same way `fmt.clock` does.

5. **[P3] 24-hour clock chosen by country, not by preference** (web/kit.mjs:134)
   - Trigger: home in Canada, Australia, India, the Philippines and so on.
   - Observed: every country except the US gets `en-GB`, which is a 24-hour clock ("14:05"). English Canada and Australia mostly use 12-hour time, and there is no setting to change it.
   - Expected: follow the system or locale hour cycle, or offer a 12/24 h setting.
   - Fix: use the system hour cycle or add a Settings toggle.

6. **[P3] Units default to miles and feet everywhere, and km labels are rounded wrongly** (web/place.mjs:63, web/app.mjs:302-303 and :313, web/kit.mjs:120)
   - Trigger: a non-US place, or switching Distance to Kilometers.
   - Observed:
     - Distance always defaults to `mi`, even for an IP place in Germany or France.
     - Radius steps stay in miles and are shown with 0 decimals, so an alert radius of 1 mi reads "2 km" when it is really 1.6 km, and 2 mi reads "3 km".
     - `fmt.int` always groups numbers the US way ("35,000").
   - Expected: km by default outside the US, UK and Myanmar, and labels that match the real radius.
   - Fix: choose the default from the place's `countryCode` on first save, show 1 decimal in km under 10, and use locale grouping.

7. **[P3] No crash reporting** (index.js:7, web/app.mjs has no handlers, src/App.tsx)
   - Trigger: any exception in the field, such as the already-known poll-loop death.
   - Observed:
     - The page has no `window.onerror` or `unhandledrejection` handler.
     - The React Native side has no ErrorBoundary.
     - `LogBox.ignoreAllLogs()` is on, and errors go only to `console.error`.
     - Combined with the known WebView-crash and poll-death issues, failures on users' TVs leave no trace.
   - Fix: add global handlers that post `{type:'error'}` to the app, keep a small ring buffer in localStorage, and show it under About.

8. **[P3] API shape change shows up as "no coverage"** (web/live.mjs:310, web/live.mjs:318)
   - Trigger: adsb.fi returns 200 without an `ac` array, for example a renamed field (the v2 API used `aircraft`) or a JSON error body.
   - Observed: `ac=[]` makes the coverage probe run. It finds no `ac` either, sets `coverage.none=true`, and the dashboard says "No receiver coverage here. The aircraft feed has no receivers near this location." That is permanent and wrong. Open-Meteo search behaves the same way: a missing `results` turns into "No places match".
   - Expected: a "feed format changed / unavailable" message.
   - Fix: treat a payload without `Array.isArray(ac)` as an error status and not as an empty sky.

9. **[P3] 1 GB stick: saved base maps also stay in RAM** (web/live.mjs:63, web/mapgen.mjs:223)
   - Trigger: stepping through map radii.
   - Observed: `store.set` keeps every value in its `memory` Map as well as in localStorage, so up to 3 base maps (one per recent radius) stay in RAM besides `maps.base`. The detail map avoids this on purpose (see the comment at mapgen.mjs:351). I did not measure the size.
   - Fix: give large values a `store.set` option that skips the memory copy, or write base maps straight to localStorage the way `saveDetail` does.

10. **[P3] First launch with no internet: the IP lookup is never retried** (web/app.mjs:685-687)
    - Trigger: the stick boots before Wi-Fi is up.
    - Observed: `locateByIp` is tried once. The screen says "We couldn't find your location automatically" and stays on manual entry. When the connection comes back, nothing retries and nothing says the problem was connectivity.
    - Fix: retry the IP lookup with back-off while the Location screen is open with no place, and word the message differently when the request failed rather than returned nothing.

**Covered with no new defect beyond the known lists**
- **Lifecycle:** the only page-side gap is the known "page never told about background". The AppState and chime gating on the native side is consistent.
- **Clock skew:** no device time-zone use anywhere. Every date or hour call passes the home `timeZone`. The remaining skew paths are already known.
- **Time zone change while running:** the device time zone is never read, so the home time zone is unaffected.
- **429 from every service at once:** ADSB.lol backs off 900 s. Every other service either fails soft or is already known (adsb.fi has no back-off, Planespotters caches the failure for 24 h, tiles leave holes, the time-zone lookup falls back silently, getBytes sends a duplicate request).
- **Old settings shapes:** `loadSettings` clamps and falls back on every field. The logbook shape is the same in every commit, and older logs without `planes` are handled. Map versions are checked. The `whatsup.map.v1` key predates the package rename, so the new package starts with empty storage.
- **Old com.bureauobscura.whatsup package:** changed in commit 2057968 (manifest.toml:7). It is a separate app with its own storage, so your test TVs will show two "What's Up" apps until the old one is uninstalled. No code still refers to the old ID.

**Areas still unexamined**
- How VoiceView behaves inside the Vega WebView (whether D-pad keys reach the page with VoiceView on, and whether DOM focus is announced) needs a device test.
- Fire TV profiles: whether Vega gives each profile its own WebView storage can't be told from the code.
- Actual memory use and low-memory-killer behaviour on a 1 GB stick at 250 mi with Atlas Satellite plus a detail map needs device profiling.
- Real suspend/resume behaviour on Vega (whether WebView timers freeze, and whether the renderer is reclaimed in the background) is not checked.
- Typing places with diacritics, apostrophes or "/" (São Paulo, St. John's, Australian unit addresses) on the A–Z keyboard against Open-Meteo, Census and Nominatim needs network tests.
- Reduced motion (Departures flaps, credit fades) is not checked.
- High-contrast, colour-filter and screen magnifier modes are not checked.
- Behaviour on 4K and 720p panels and with overscan is not checked.
- Audio focus and the chime when another app or Alexa is speaking is not checked.
- Factory reset and app-update upgrade paths through the Appstore (data kept or wiped) are not checked.
- Captive-portal or DNS-hijack networks, where requests return HTML with a 200 status, are not checked.
